definition: With even stronger reason; used in legal argument to indicate that a conclusion follows even more strongly from a stronger premise.
plainEnglish: 'Even more so'—if X is true, then Y is even more obviously true.

definition: To escape, flee or disappear.

A pardon which frees the criminal without any condition whatever from reaches both the punishment prescribed for the offense and the guilt of the offender. It obliterates in legal contemplation of the offense itself. It restores the accused to his civil rights and remits the penalty imposed for the particular offense of which he was convicted in so far as it remains unpaid or unserved.
A standard of appellate review requiring the appellant to show that the lower court's decision was arbitrary, unreasonable, or based on an erroneous view of the law.
plainEnglish: Reversing a trial judge only if they got it really wrong, not just because the appeals court would have decided differently.

definition: A tort consisting of using a legal process primarily for an ulterior purpose not intended by the law, even if the process itself was originally proper.
plainEnglish: Misusing a legal procedure (even a legitimate one) for an improper purpose.

definition: A manifestation of assent to the terms of an offer, made in the manner invited or required by the offer.
plainEnglish: Saying yes to a deal in the way the offer required.

definition: A person who aids or contributes in a secondary way or assists in or contributes to a crime as a subordinate; an accessory does acts which facilitate others in the commission or attempted commission of a crime or in avoiding apprehension for a crime.
One who receives, comforts, or assists a felon knowing that he has committed a felony, or is sought in connection with the commission of a felony.
One who procures, counsels or commands the deed perpetrated, but who is not actively present at such perpetration.
A person who knowingly assists or encourages another to commit a crime, sharing in the principal's criminal intent.
plainEnglish: Someone who helps another person commit a crime.

definition: To come into existence as a legal claim, typically when all elements of the cause of action are present; the moment from which the statute of limitations begins to run.
plainEnglish: When a legal claim officially comes into existence—the clock for suing starts here.

definition: A person against whom a criminal proceeding is initiated, charging him with the commission of a crime or punishable offense.
A formal declaration before a notary or other official that the signer executed a document voluntarily; required for many recorded documents.
plainEnglish: Formally confirming to a notary that you signed a document on purpose.

definition: To find a defendant not guilty in a criminal trial.
A judgment by a court or jury that a defendant is not guilty of the crime charged.
plainEnglish: A finding of not guilty.

definition: A judge in the full-time service of the court. Compare to senior judge.
The physical act or unlawful conduct required to constitute a crime; literally 'guilty act.'
plainEnglish: The 'guilty act'—the physical thing the person did.

definition: For this purpose; created for a specific, immediate need rather than general application.
plainEnglish: 'For this'—made for one specific situation.

definition: For the purposes of the lawsuit; a guardian ad litem, for instance, is appointed to represent a party only for the duration of a case.
plainEnglish: 'For the lawsuit'—appointed only for this case.

definition: Something to be added, especially to a document; a supplement.
To decide or make a judicial judgment or order.

term: Administrative Office of the United States Courts
definition: The federal agency responsible for collecting court statistics, administering the federal courts' budget, and performing many other administrative and programmatic functions, under the direction and supervision of the Judicial Conference of the United States.
A person appointed by the court to administer the estate of a person who died without a will or whose will did not name an executor.
plainEnglish: Court-appointed person who handles the estate when there's no will (or no named executor).

definition: A term used to describe evidence that may be considered by a jury or judge in civil and criminal cases.
A statement by a party acknowledging the truth of a fact, admissible against them.
plainEnglish: When a party concedes a fact as true.

definition: To acknowledge the truth of a fact or allegation, often in a pleading or response.
plainEnglish: To agree that a fact is true.

definition: The legal process by which an adult assumes the parental rights and responsibilities of a child not biologically their own.
plainEnglish: Legally becoming a parent to a child who wasn't biologically yours.

definition: A document specifying a person's healthcare wishes if they become unable to communicate, such as a living will or healthcare proxy.
plainEnglish: A document saying what medical care you want if you can't communicate.

definition: One having opposing parties; contested, as distinguished from a hearing in which only one party appears.
The acquisition of title to land by openly occupying it for a statutory period in a manner hostile to the true owner's rights.
plainEnglish: Gaining ownership of land by using it openly and without permission long enough.

definition: A written statement of facts sworn to under oath before an authorized officer such as a notary.
plainEnglish: A sworn written statement.

definition: A sworn statement confirming that a particular document was served on a designated party in a specified manner.
plainEnglish: A sworn statement proving papers were served.

definition: To ratify, make firm, confirm, establish, reassert. Alternate to swearing under an oath.
A judicial proceeding in which a party seeks to confirm or ratify that a valid marriage exists between that party and the other party to the suit.
A defense that, even if the plaintiff's allegations are true, defeats or mitigates the claim, such as statute of limitations or self-defense.
plainEnglish: 'Even if everything you say is true, I still win because of X.'

definition: In the practice of the court of appeals, it means that the court of appeals has concluded that the lower court decision is correct and will stand as rendered by the lower court.
Premeditated or conceived of before actually being done or carried out.

To assault where serious bodily injury is inflicted on the person assaulted; it is also an assault with the intent to commit an additional crime, such as rape, murder or robbery; it also includes assaults committed with deadly weapons.
One whose legal right is invaded by an act complained of.
To actively, knowingly, intentionally, or purposefully facilitate or assist another individual in the commission or attempted commission of a crime.

A plea of guilty despite a claim of innocence by a defendant who acknowledges that the evidence may be sufficient to convict him, named for the case of North Carolina v. Alford; an Alford plea is a guilty plea.
A name, other than his true name, by which a person is known; an indication that person is known by more than one name, often shown with the abbreviation AKA (also known as).
A defense proving that the accused, at the time of the commission of the crime charged, was at a different place than the scene of the crime, so that he could not possibly have committed it.
Court-ordered financial support paid by one ex-spouse to the other after a divorce or separation.
plainEnglish: Spousal support paid after divorce.

definition: A statement or claim of fact made by a party in a pleading, asserted as true but yet to be proven.
plainEnglish: A formal claim made in a lawsuit that hasn't been proven yet.

definition: To assert, declare, or state a fact in a pleading without yet having proved it.
plainEnglish: To formally claim something is true (without yet proving it).

definition: Presentence step in which the judge asks the defendant whether he has any legal cause to show why judgment should not be pronounced against him, or whether he would like to make statement on his behalf and present any information in mitigation of sentence. It permits defendants to speak in their own behalf in criminal cases prior to sentencing and to present any information in mitigation of punishment procedure.
A juror selected in the same manner as a regular juror who hears all the evidence but does not help decide the case unless called on to replace a regular juror.
A procedure for settling a dispute outside the courtroom. Most forms of ADR are not binding, and involve referral of the case to a neutral party such as an arbitrator or mediator.
To change.
A 'friend of the court'—a non-party who, with leave of court, files a brief offering information or argument relevant to the case.
plainEnglish: An outsider, usually an organization, who weighs in on a case they're not actually a party to.

definition: One growing out of or auxiliary to another action or suit, or which is subordinate to or in aid of a primary action, either law or in chancery.
Any process which is in aid of or incidental to the principal suit or action; e.g. attachment.
A judicial declaration that a marriage was invalid from the start, as distinguished from divorce, which terminates a valid marriage.
plainEnglish: A court ruling that the marriage was never legally valid.

definition: The defendant's formal written response to the complaint, admitting or denying each allegation and raising any affirmative defenses.
plainEnglish: The defendant's official reply to the lawsuit.

definition: A clear and unequivocal indication by one party, before performance is due, that they will not perform the contract.
plainEnglish: Telling the other side in advance that you won't be keeping your end of the deal.

definition: A request to a higher court to review and change the decision of a lower court.
plainEnglish: Asking a higher court to overturn the lower court's ruling.

definition: A formal proceeding by which a party summoned submits or presents himself to the court.
The party who appeals a lower court's decision to a higher court.
plainEnglish: The party challenging the lower court's ruling on appeal.

definition: About appeals; an appellate court has the power to review the judgment of a lower court (trial court) or tribunal. For example, the U.S. circuit courts of appeals review the decisions of the U.S. district courts.

The power vested in an appellate court to review and revise the judicial action of an inferior court, evidenced by an appellate order or an appealable judgment rendered by such court. Limits of appellate jurisdiction are governed by statutes or constitutions. For example, the Court of Appeals has appellate jurisdiction over criminal cases (except capital murder cases) tried in circuit courts.
The party against whom an appeal is taken; the party defending the lower court's decision.
plainEnglish: The party defending the lower court's ruling on appeal.

definition: A process where parties submit a dispute to a neutral third party (arbitrator) whose decision is typically binding and enforceable, often pursuant to a contractual arbitration clause.
plainEnglish: A private alternative to court where an arbitrator decides the case—usually binding.

definition: To present reasons for or against a position, especially in oral argument before a court.
plainEnglish: To make your case to a judge.

definition: A reasoned set of points presented to a court in support of a legal position, in writing or orally.
plainEnglish: Your reasoning presented to the court.

definition: Arraignment of an accused consists of calling upon him by name, reading to him the charges in the arrest documents, demanding of him whether he pleads guilty or not guilty or, in misdemeanors, nolo contendere, and entering his plea. This hearing may be combined with right to counsel hearing.
A court proceeding where a defendant is formally charged, informed of the charges, and asked to enter a plea.
plainEnglish: The first court appearance where the defendant hears the charges and enters a plea.

definition: That which is unpaid although due to be paid; a person "in arrears" is behind in payment.
To deprive a person of his liberty by legal authority; to take a person who is suspected of a crime into official custody.
The illegal and malicious burning or destruction of any dwelling.
A federal judge who is appointed for life, during "good behavior," under Article III of the Constitution. Article III judges are nominated by the President and confirmed by the Senate.
An intentional act that causes another person to reasonably apprehend imminent harmful or offensive contact.
plainEnglish: Making someone reasonably fear they're about to be physically hurt.

definition: To state or claim a right, defense, or position formally.
plainEnglish: To formally claim or insist on something.

definition: Property of all kinds, including real and personal, tangible and intangible.
The transfer of contractual rights from one party (assignor) to a third party (assignee).
plainEnglish: Handing off your right to receive something under a contract to someone else.

definition: A defense barring recovery when the plaintiff knowingly and voluntarily accepted a known risk that caused the injury.
plainEnglish: You knew it was dangerous and did it anyway, so you can't sue.

definition: An employment relationship that either employer or employee may end at any time, with or without cause, subject to legal exceptions.
plainEnglish: Employment that either side can end at any time, for almost any reason.

definition: A court-ordered seizure of a defendant's property to secure a potential judgment, typically before trial.
plainEnglish: Court-ordered seizure of property to secure a possible judgment.

definition: An inchoate crime consisting of an intent to commit a specific offense plus a substantial step toward its commission.
plainEnglish: Trying to commit a crime but not actually completing it.

definition: A lawyer or counsel; a person who is qualified and authorized to assist and to represent people in legal matters, including in the trying of cases and suits in court.

The chief law officer of the federal government or of each state government; his office represents the government and its agencies in court; his office also represents the people of the state and assists district attorneys in the prosecution of criminal cases.
A privilege protecting confidential communications between a lawyer and client made for the purpose of obtaining legal advice.
plainEnglish: Things you say to your lawyer in confidence can't be used against you.

definition: A person, not necessarily a lawyer, to whom authority is given by another to act in his place. The authority to act as an Attorney-In-Fact is given by a document containing a power or letter of attorney.
The process of establishing that a document, recording, or other evidence is what it purports to be, a prerequisite to admissibility.
plainEnglish: Proving that a document or item is actually what you say it is.

definition: An injunction that automatically takes effect upon filing a bankruptcy petition, halting most collection efforts and lawsuits against the debtor.
plainEnglish: An instant freeze on collection efforts the moment someone files for bankruptcy.

definition: To assert formally, especially in a pleading; to allege as a matter of fact.
plainEnglish: A formal way of saying 'state' or 'claim,' usually in court papers.

definition: A positive statement of fact in a pleading, asserted as true.
plainEnglish: A formal assertion of fact in a court document.

definition: Dishonest or unfair conduct, especially the deliberate breach of the duty of good faith and fair dealing in contracts.
plainEnglish: Acting dishonestly or unfairly, often deliberately.

definition: Money or property pledged to the court to secure a defendant's release from custody and ensure their appearance at trial.
plainEnglish: Money or property put up to get out of jail before trial, forfeited if the defendant skips court.

definition: A document executed to obtain the release of a person in custody stating that the surety forfeits his security in the event the defendant fails to appear as required for court dates.
Loss of bail status by order of a judge, usually upon a defendant's failure to appear.
A court officer responsible for maintaining order in the courtroom, calling witnesses, and attending to the needs of the judge and jury.
plainEnglish: The court officer who keeps order in the courtroom.

definition: A legal procedure for dealing with debt problems of individuals and businesses; specifically, a case filed under one of the chapters of title 11 of the United States Code (the Bankruptcy Code).

An officer of the Judiciary serving in the judicial districts of Alabama and North Carolina who, like the United States trustee, is responsible for supervising the administration of bankruptcy cases, estates, and trustees; monitoring plans and disclosure statements; monitoring creditors' committees; monitoring fee applications; and performing other statutory duties.
The informal name for title 11 of the United States Code (11 U.S.C. §§ 101-1330), the federal bankruptcy law.
The bankruptcy judges in regular active service in each district; a unit of the district court.
All interests of the debtor in property at the time of the bankruptcy filing. The estate technically becomes the temporary legal owner of all of the debtor's property.
A judicial officer of the United States district court who is the court official with decision-making power over federal bankruptcy cases.
A formal request for the protection of the federal bankruptcy laws. (There is an official form for bankruptcy petitions.)
A private individual or corporation appointed in all Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 cases to represent the interests of the bankruptcy estate and the debtor's creditors.
The legal profession as a whole, or the licensing body governing it; also, the railing separating the public area of a courtroom.
plainEnglish: The legal profession or its licensing body.

definition: An intentional, harmful or offensive contact with another person without their consent.
plainEnglish: Intentionally touching someone in a harmful or offensive way without permission.

definition: A trial in which the judge, not a jury, determines both the facts and the law.
plainEnglish: A trial decided by a judge alone, no jury.

definition: An arrest warrant issued by the court.
A person designated to receive property under a will, trust, life insurance policy, or similar arrangement.
plainEnglish: The person who gets something under a will, trust, or policy.

definition: A gift of personal property made by will.
plainEnglish: A gift of personal property in a will.

definition: A rule requiring the original document (or a reliable duplicate) to prove its contents, rather than testimony about the document.
plainEnglish: If you want to prove what a document says, you generally have to produce the document itself.

definition: The legal standard guiding decisions in child custody, visitation, and adoption matters, focused on the child's welfare rather than the parents' preferences.
plainEnglish: The rule that says decisions about kids should put the kid's well-being first.

definition: The highest standard of proof, required to convict in criminal cases; doubt based on reason after considering all the evidence.
plainEnglish: The high bar prosecutors have to clear to convict—no reasonable doubt that the defendant did it.

definition: The pleading filed in equity actions.
A certified, itemized statement of the amount of costs in an action or suit.
A formal written document accusing a person or persons named of having committed a felony or misdemeanor, lawfully presented by the prosecuting attorney for their action upon it.
A written statement or specification of the details of the demand for which an action at law is brought.
Legal authority that a court is required to follow, such as decisions of higher courts in the same jurisdiction.
plainEnglish: Law a court has to follow.

definition: In good faith; genuine, sincere, and without intent to deceive.
plainEnglish: 'In good faith'—legitimate and honest.

definition: A buyer who acquires property in good faith, for value, and without notice of competing claims, often gaining superior title.
plainEnglish: Someone who buys property in good faith, paying real money, without knowing about any other claims to it.

definition: A written obligation to pay a sum or perform an act, often required to secure court-ordered duties such as appearance, performance, or appeal.
plainEnglish: A written promise (often backed by money) to pay or appear.

definition: Failure to meet a legal duty or obligation, whether in tort (breach of duty of care) or contract (breach of promise).
plainEnglish: Failing to do what you were legally required to do.

definition: A written legal document submitted to a court arguing the law and facts in support of a party's position on a motion, appeal, or other issue.
plainEnglish: A formal written argument submitted to the court.

definition: The obligation of a party to prove disputed facts to a specified level of certainty, encompassing both the burden of production and the burden of persuasion.
plainEnglish: Whose job it is to prove what, and how convincingly.

definition: The entering into a house or building or structure with the intent of committing a felony or a theft therein.
A bankruptcy case in which the debtor is a business or an individual involved in business and the debts are for business purposes.
A presumption that corporate directors acted on an informed basis, in good faith, and in the honest belief their actions were in the company's best interest.
plainEnglish: Courts give corporate directors the benefit of the doubt on business decisions made in good faith.

definition: Actual cause—the harm would not have occurred but for the defendant's conduct.
plainEnglish: If the defendant hadn't done it, this harm wouldn't have happened.

definition: General name for a court order requiring law enforcement to take a person into custody.
A crime punishable by death.
A sentence of death for the convicted offender.
The heading of a court document identifying the court, parties, case number, and document title.
plainEnglish: The header on a court document showing the case name and number.

definition: A complete collection of every document filed in court in a case.
The law as established in previous court decisions. A synonym for legal precedent. Akin to common law, which springs from tradition and judicial decisions.
The number of cases handled by a judge or a court.
The causal link between a defendant's conduct and the plaintiff's harm, generally requiring both actual cause and proximate cause.
plainEnglish: Proving the defendant's conduct actually caused the harm.

definition: The factual link between conduct and harm, typically shown by the but-for test or, in some cases, the substantial factor test.
plainEnglish: The factual showing that the defendant's act actually caused the harm.

definition: The legal basis for a lawsuit—the facts and legal theory that entitle a plaintiff to a remedy from a defendant.
plainEnglish: The legal reason for the lawsuit—the theory and facts that justify suing.

definition: A warning or caution; in legal practice, often a formal notice filed to delay or prevent action.
plainEnglish: A warning or qualifier.

definition: Let the buyer beware—the principle that buyers must inspect goods and bear the risk of defects unless protected by warranty or statute.
plainEnglish: 'Let the buyer beware'—you bought it, you live with it.

definition: A writ by which a higher court reviews a lower court's decision; the U.S. Supreme Court grants certiorari to take a case.
plainEnglish: The way a higher court agrees to review a lower court's decision—Supreme Court 'cert.'

definition: The chronological documentation of the seizure, transfer, and handling of physical evidence to ensure its integrity and admissibility.
plainEnglish: The paper trail showing who had the evidence and when—proving it wasn't tampered with.

definition: A request to remove a prospective juror based on a specific reason such as bias or inability to be impartial.
plainEnglish: Striking a juror with a stated, valid reason.

definition: The offices of a judge and his or her staff.
A term used to identify equity cases in which the party filing suit is seeking an award of something other than money.
The chancery docket lists all chancery cases in the sequence in which they were filed and generally refer to pending cases only.

These books contain a copy of all orders (both interlocutory and final) entered in equity cases. They are recorded in the date order in which they were entered in the court, not batched together with other orders in the same case.
A reorganization bankruptcy, typically used by businesses, allowing the debtor to continue operating while restructuring debts under court supervision.
plainEnglish: Business reorganization bankruptcy—the company keeps running while it restructures its debts.

definition: A consumer bankruptcy reorganization allowing individuals with regular income to repay debts over three to five years under a court-approved plan.
plainEnglish: Individual repayment-plan bankruptcy—you keep your stuff but pay off debts over 3-5 years.

definition: A liquidation bankruptcy under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in which a trustee gathers and sells the debtor's nonexempt property to pay creditors.
plainEnglish: 'Wipe-out' bankruptcy—non-exempt assets are sold off and most debts are discharged.

definition: Evidence of a person's character or character trait, generally inadmissible to prove conduct on a particular occasion but admissible for other purposes.
plainEnglish: Evidence about someone's general character (good or bad), usually not allowed to prove they did something.

definition: A formal accusation of a crime; also, the judge's instructions to the jury on the law.
plainEnglish: The formal accusation of a crime; or, the judge's instructions to the jury.

definition: The judge who has primary responsibility for the administration of a court; chief judges are determined by seniority.
Court-ordered payments made by a non-custodial parent to the custodial parent for the support of their child.
plainEnglish: Payments by one parent to the other for the kids' expenses.

definition: A geographical area containing one or more courts.

Indirect evidence; the evidence of facts or circumstances from which the existence or non-existence of other facts or circumstances may be inferred; the showing of secondary facts by which a principal fact may be rationally inferred.

A written order requiring the appearance of a person at the time and place indicated therein; it may be issued instead of taking the person under arrest; if the person fails to appear, then an arrest warrant may be issued.
An action seeking monetary damages or asking for equitable relief.

A type of contempt of court which generally arises from a willful failure to comply with an order of the court such as an injunction as contrasted with criminal contempt which consists generally of contumelious conduct in the presence of the court.
A listing of all pending civil actions, whether “legal” or “equitable” in nature.
A legal system based on comprehensive codified statutes (as in continental Europe and Louisiana); also, the body of law dealing with private rights as opposed to criminal law.
plainEnglish: Either: a code-based legal system; or: the law of private disputes (as opposed to criminal).

definition: The Civil Order Book contains a copy of all orders (both interlocutory and final) entered in civil cases. The orders are recorded in the date order in which they were entered in the court, not batched together with other orders in the same case.
An assertion of a legal right or demand for relief; also, the underlying basis for a lawsuit.
plainEnglish: A demand for something you say you're legally entitled to.

definition: A lawsuit in which one or more plaintiffs sue on behalf of a larger group of similarly situated people.
plainEnglish: One lawsuit brought by a few people on behalf of many.

definition: An intermediate standard of proof requiring a high probability of truth, used in certain civil matters such as fraud, termination of parental rights, and punitive damages.
plainEnglish: Higher than 'more likely than not' but lower than 'beyond a reasonable doubt.'

definition: Court administrative personnel who assists the court and manages the daily operations of the court.
A summary of the evidence presented to the jury by the attorneys.
A systematic compilation of statutes, often arranged by subject, such as the U.S. Code or a state's statutory code.
plainEnglish: An organized collection of statutes by topic.

definition: A supplement or addition to an existing will, modifying or revoking part of it without replacing it entirely.
plainEnglish: An amendment to a will.

definition: To arrange and incorporate laws into a systematic code or to enact a rule of common law into statutory form.
plainEnglish: To put rules into a written, organized code.

definition: An involuntary confession which is usually inadmissable because it was obtained by threats or force.
Property pledged to secure a debt, which the creditor may seize if the debtor defaults.
plainEnglish: Property you put up to back a loan—the lender can take it if you don't pay.

definition: The doctrine that prevents a party from relitigating an issue of fact or law that was actually litigated and necessarily decided in a prior action.
plainEnglish: You can't re-fight a specific issue that's already been decided in an earlier case.

definition: The constitutional provision (Article I, § 8) granting Congress the power to regulate commerce with foreign nations, among the states, and with Indian tribes.
plainEnglish: The part of the Constitution that gives Congress power to regulate business and commerce.

definition: A lawyer appointed by the chief circuit court judge who conducts evidentiary hearings and makes factual findings in circuit court cases referred to him by the circuit court judge who is conducting the trial. The Commissioner in Chancery collects a fee for his services. His findings of fact are subject to challenge before the circuit court judge through the “noting of exceptions” by the objecting lawyer or an unrepresented party, which results in a hearing and re-examination of the evidence by the judge.
The body of law derived from judicial decisions rather than statutes, developed over time through case-by-case adjudication.
plainEnglish: Law made by judges through decisions, rather than written by legislatures.

definition: An offense, which is defined by common law rather than by statute.
A special condition the court imposes that requires an individual to work – without pay – for a civic or nonprofit organization.
A doctrine that reduces a plaintiff's damages in proportion to their own degree of fault in causing the injury.
plainEnglish: Plaintiff's recovery is reduced based on how much they were at fault too.

definition: Damages awarded to make the injured party whole by reimbursing actual losses, including economic and non-economic harm.
plainEnglish: Money meant to put the victim back where they would have been.

definition: Judicial determination as to whether the criminal (competency to stand trial) defendant sufficiently understands the nature of trial proceedings.
The initial pleading filed by a plaintiff that states the basis for the lawsuit, the legal claims, and the relief sought.
plainEnglish: The document that starts a lawsuit, explaining what happened and what the plaintiff wants.

definition: A sentence imposed which is to be served at the same time as another sentence imposed earlier or at the same time.
A separate opinion by a judge agreeing with the result of the majority but offering different or additional reasoning.
plainEnglish: A judge who agrees with the outcome but for different reasons.

definition: An admission of guilt or other incriminating statement made by the accused, either orally or in writing.

Arises when a criminal defense attorney represents more than one client; because the codefendant's interests or defenses may be dissimilar or incompatible, counsel will ask to be relieved from representing one of the defendants; when such a conflict is declared, private counsel is appointed by the court to represent him.

Separate sentences (each additional to the others) imposed upon a defendant who has been convicted for several distinct offenses; one of such sentences being made to begin at the expiration of another.
A person appointed by the court to manage the financial affairs or personal care of someone who cannot do so themselves.
plainEnglish: Court-appointed person who manages another's money or personal care.

definition: Something of value (an act, forbearance, or promise) bargained for and given in exchange for a promise, required to make a contract enforceable.
plainEnglish: The 'something for something'—each side has to give up or do something for the deal to count.

definition: Joining of separate cases together under one case number.
Unification of two or more actions.

The act or process of uniting several actions into one trial and judgment, by order of the court, where all actions are between the same parties, pending in the same court and involving substantially the same subject matter.
An agreement between two or more persons to commit an unlawful act, typically requiring an overt act in furtherance.
plainEnglish: A plot between two or more people to commit a crime.

definition: Notice imputed by law to a person based on information that could have been discovered through reasonable inquiry, such as recorded documents.
plainEnglish: Notice you're treated as having even if you didn't actually know, because the information was publicly available.

definition: To put together; to arrange or marshal the words of an instrument. As with a will—to ascertain the meaning of language by a process of arrangement and inference.
A bankruptcy case filed to reduce or eliminate debts that are primarily consumer debts.
Debts incurred for personal, as opposed to business, needs.
Any act which is calculated to embarrass, hinder, or obstruct the court in administration of justice, or which is calculated to lessen its authority or its dignity.
Conduct that defies the authority of a court, such as disobeying an order or disrupting proceedings; may be civil or criminal.
plainEnglish: Disobeying or disrespecting the court—you can be jailed or fined for it.

definition: To argue or assert a particular position, especially in a legal proceeding.
plainEnglish: To argue a particular point.

definition: A claim that may be owed by the debtor under certain circumstances, e.g., where the debtor is a cosigner on another person's loan and that person fails to pay.
The adjournment or postponement of an action or proceeding pending in a court until some future date.
A legally enforceable agreement between two or more parties, typically requiring offer, acceptance, consideration, and mutual assent.
plainEnglish: A legally binding deal.

definition: A common-law doctrine, now largely replaced by comparative negligence, that bars a plaintiff from recovery if they were even slightly at fault.
plainEnglish: Old rule—if the plaintiff was at all to blame, they get nothing.

definition: The wrongful exercise of control over another's personal property to the extent that justifies forcing payment of full value.
plainEnglish: Treating someone else's property as your own—the civil version of theft.

definition: A judgment finding a defendant guilty of a criminal offense.
plainEnglish: A finding of guilty.

definition: The exclusive legal right of an author or creator to reproduce, distribute, perform, and adapt an original work of authorship for a limited time.
plainEnglish: The exclusive rights of an author or creator over their work.

definition: A public official who investigates the causes and circumstances of deaths that occur within his jurisdiction, especially to determine whether the death was not by natural causes.
A legal entity created under state law that is separate from its owners (shareholders) and has rights and obligations distinct from those of the individuals who form it.
plainEnglish: A business treated by the law as its own 'person,' separate from the people who own it.

definition: An essential element of a criminal offense which must be proved by the district attorney; specifically, the prosecution must prove that a death occurred and it is the result of murder.
Legal advice; a term also used to refer to the lawyers in a case.
A separate and distinct charge or claim in a charging document, each capable of supporting independent conviction or liability.
plainEnglish: Each separate charge in an indictment or complaint.

definition: A claim brought by a defendant against a plaintiff in the same lawsuit, asserting that the plaintiff is liable to the defendant.
plainEnglish: The defendant's own lawsuit against the plaintiff, filed inside the same case.

definition: A facility run by a county to detain people awaiting trial or convicted and sentenced for minor crimes or offenses.
Government entity authorized to resolve legal disputes. Judges sometimes use "court" to refer to themselves in the third person, as in "the court has read the briefs."
A command or mandatory direction of a judge which is made during a case. Also includes a command of the judge which establishes courtroom or administrative procedures.

A person who makes a word-for-word record of what is said in court, generally by using a stenographic machine, shorthand or audio recording, and then produces a transcript of the proceedings upon request.
Trial by a judge alone without a jury.

Generally refers to two events in individual bankruptcy cases: (1) the "individual or group briefing" from a nonprofit budget and credit counseling agency that individual debtors must attend prior to filing under any chapter of the Bankruptcy Code; and (2) the "instructional course in personal financial management" in chapters 7 and 13 that an individual debtor must complete before a discharge is entered. There are exceptions to both requirements for certain categories of debtors, exigent circumstances, or if the U.S. trustee or bankruptcy administrator have determined that there are insufficient approved credit counseling agencies available to provide the necessary counseling.
A person to whom or business to which the debtor owes money or that claims to be owed money by the debtor.
Any act which the sovereign power of a country has deemed contrary to the public good and hence, prosecutable in a criminal proceeding; crimes include "felonies" and "misdemeanors".
The body of law defining offenses against the state and prescribing punishment.
plainEnglish: The law dealing with crimes.

definition: Questioning by a lawyer of a witness for the opposing side.
A claim brought by one party against a co-party (e.g., one defendant against another defendant) in the same lawsuit.
plainEnglish: When co-defendants (or co-plaintiffs) sue each other within the same case.

definition: The questioning of a witness by the opposing party after direct examination, designed to test credibility and elicit favorable facts.
plainEnglish: The other side's chance to question your witness.

definition: A parent's legal authority and responsibility regarding the care, control, and decision-making for a child, split between legal custody and physical custody.
plainEnglish: Who has the right to make decisions for and live with a child.

definition: The type of proceedings in which the court determines which parent, other adult, or agency shall have physical control over a child.
Monetary compensation awarded to a party who has suffered harm or loss due to another's wrongful act.
plainEnglish: Money the wrongdoer has to pay the injured party.

definition: The federal standard for admissibility of expert testimony, requiring the trial judge to determine whether the expert's methodology is scientifically reliable and relevant.
plainEnglish: Federal courts' test for whether an expert's methods are reliable enough to testify.

definition: In fact, as a matter of practice, regardless of official status; often contrasted with de jure.
plainEnglish: 'In reality'—what's actually happening, even if it's not official.

definition: By law, as a matter of legal right; often contrasted with de facto.
plainEnglish: 'By law'—what the law officially says, even if reality differs.

definition: A standard of appellate review in which the higher court considers the matter anew, without deference to the lower court's conclusions on issues of law.
plainEnglish: The appeals court looks at it fresh, without giving weight to what the trial court decided.

definition: A new hearing or a hearing for the second time contemplating an entire trial in the same manner in which the matter was originally heard. Court hears matter as court of original jurisdiction and not appellate jurisdiction.
Time spent by defendant in jail awaiting trial and sentencing.
A debtor's detailed description of how the debtor proposes to pay creditors' claims over a fixed period of time.
A written statement made under penalty of perjury, similar to an affidavit but not requiring a notary in many jurisdictions.
plainEnglish: A written statement made under penalty of perjury—like an affidavit but no notary required.

definition: A judge's statement about someone's rights. For example, a plaintiff may seek a declaratory judgment that a particular statute, as written, violates some constitutional right.
The judgment of a court of equity. It is the equivalent to an Order (just a different name).
A legal document transferring ownership of real property from one party to another.
plainEnglish: The legal document that transfers ownership of real estate.

definition: A false statement of fact communicated to a third party that damages the reputation of the subject.
plainEnglish: Saying or writing something false that damages someone's reputation.

definition: Failure to perform a legal duty, such as paying a debt or appearing in court when required.
plainEnglish: Failing to do what you were required to do (pay, appear in court, etc.).

definition: A judgment entered against a party who fails to plead or otherwise defend an action.
plainEnglish: Winning automatically because the other side didn't show up or respond.

definition: The party against whom a lawsuit is brought and who must respond to the plaintiff's allegations.
plainEnglish: The person being sued (or charged, in a criminal case).

definition: The transfer of contractual duties to a third party, though the delegating party generally remains liable for performance.
plainEnglish: Handing off your duties under a contract to someone else (though you're still on the hook).

definition: Jury discussions and consideration of the facts conducted prior to reaching a decision.

A pleading by a defendant disputing the legal sufficiency of plaintiff's pleadings. In effect, it is an allegation that “even if the plaintiff's claims are true, he has not stated a claim which is sufficient for the judge to enter an order in his favor for the requested award.” It is used to try to get a case dismissed because the legal claims are not sufficient for granting judicial relief.
A defendant's refusal in a pleading to admit the truth of an allegation.
plainEnglish: The defendant's 'not true' response in an answer.

definition: To refuse to admit the truth of an allegation in a pleading.
plainEnglish: To say 'not true' to an allegation in a complaint.

definition: Sworn out-of-court testimony of a witness, taken under oath and recorded for use in pretrial discovery or at trial.
plainEnglish: An interview under oath, recorded by a court reporter, used to lock in a witness's story.

definition: To hold a suspect or suspect's property against that suspects will.
A gift of real property made by will; historically distinguished from bequest of personal property.
plainEnglish: A gift of real estate in a will.

definition: Statements in a judicial opinion that are not necessary to the decision and therefore not binding as precedent.
plainEnglish: Things a court says in an opinion that aren't the actual rule of the case—not binding.

definition: The initial questioning of a witness by the party who called them, eliciting the witness's account of the facts.
plainEnglish: The first round of questioning by the side that called the witness.

definition: The revocation of an attorney's license to practice law, the most severe disciplinary sanction.
plainEnglish: The most severe punishment for lawyer misconduct—losing your license.

definition: A court order in bankruptcy releasing the debtor from personal liability for most pre-petition debts.
plainEnglish: The bankruptcy court wiping out your debts.

definition: A debt for which the Bankruptcy Code allows the debtor's personal liability to be eliminated.

A written document prepared by the chapter 11 debtor or other plan proponent that is designed to provide "adequate information" to creditors to enable them to evaluate the chapter 11 plan of reorganization.
The pretrial process by which parties exchange information and evidence relevant to the case through depositions, interrogatories, document requests, and admissions.
plainEnglish: The phase before trial where each side digs up information from the other.

definition: A rule delaying the start of the statute of limitations until the plaintiff knew or reasonably should have known of the injury and its cause.
plainEnglish: The rule that the clock to sue starts when you discover (or should have discovered) the injury.

definition: Adverse treatment based on a protected characteristic such as race, sex, religion, national origin, age, or disability, prohibited under various civil rights statutes.
plainEnglish: Treating people worse because of a protected characteristic like race or sex.

definition: An order disposing of an action, suit, etc., without trial.
Court action that prevents an identical lawsuit from being filed later.
Court action that allows the later filing.

Income not reasonably necessary for the maintenance or support of the debtor or dependents. If the debtor operates a business, disposable income is defined as those amounts over and above what is necessary for the payment of ordinary operating expenses.
Determination of the final arrangement or settlement of a case following judgement.
A separate opinion by a judge disagreeing with the majority's result, reasoning, or both.
plainEnglish: A judge's opinion saying the majority got it wrong.

definition: The suspension of criminal prosecution of certain offenders; the offender may be asked to participate in a treatment or supervisory program in exchange for his agreement to stop or to suspend prosecution.
The legal dissolution of a valid marriage, restoring the parties to single status.
plainEnglish: Legally ending a marriage.

definition: The official record of proceedings and filings in a case, or the list of cases pending before a court.
plainEnglish: The running list of everything filed and done in a case.

definition: The Fifth Amendment protection against being tried twice for the same offense by the same sovereign.
plainEnglish: You can't be tried twice for the same crime in the same jurisdiction.

definition: The constitutional guarantee that the government will not deprive a person of life, liberty, or property without fair procedures and substantive fairness.
plainEnglish: The government has to play fair before taking your life, freedom, or property.

definition: An unlawful threat or coercion that overcomes a person's free will, making a contract voidable.
plainEnglish: Forcing someone to sign a contract by threatening them.

definition: A legal obligation owed by one person to another, breach of which can give rise to liability in tort.
plainEnglish: A legal obligation you owe to someone else (like to drive carefully).

definition: A hearsay exception for statements made by a declarant who believes death is imminent, concerning the cause or circumstances of impending death.
plainEnglish: What someone says when they think they're dying—admissible despite hearsay rules.

definition: Discovery of information stored electronically, including emails, files, and metadata, governed by special rules and procedures.
plainEnglish: Discovery of electronic stuff—emails, files, metadata.

definition: A nonpossessory right to use another's land for a specific purpose, such as a right of way.
plainEnglish: A legal right to use part of someone else's land for a specific purpose.

definition: An easement that benefits a particular parcel of land (the dominant tenement) and burdens another (the servient tenement), running with the land.
plainEnglish: An easement tied to a specific parcel—stays with the land when sold.

definition: An easement that benefits a particular person or entity rather than a parcel of land (such as a utility easement).
plainEnglish: An easement that benefits a person or company, not a piece of land.

definition: Fraudulently using or taking another's funds.
The government's power to take private property for public use, subject to payment of just compensation.
plainEnglish: The government's power to take private property for public use (paying fair value for it).

definition: French, meaning "on the bench." All judges of an appellate court sitting together to hear a case, as opposed to the routine disposition by panels of three judges. In the Ninth Circuit, an en banc panel consists of 11 randomly selected judges.

Binding claim or liability attached to real property. Encumbrances are generally liens which affect the title to the property or restrictions which affect the physical use of property, such as easements or encroachments.
A signature on a negotiable instrument transferring it or guaranteeing payment; also, an amendment to a policy or contract.
plainEnglish: Signing the back of a check or note to transfer it; or, an add-on to a policy.

definition: A defense that the defendant was induced by law enforcement to commit a crime they would not otherwise have committed.
plainEnglish: When the police talk you into committing a crime you wouldn't have committed on your own.

definition: Signing of order or decree by judge.
The Fourteenth Amendment guarantee that the government will not deny any person within its jurisdiction the equal protection of the laws.
plainEnglish: The government has to treat similarly situated people similarly.

definition: Pertaining to civil suits in "equity" rather than in "law." In English legal history, the courts of "law" could order the payment of damages and could afford no other remedy (see damages). A separate court of "equity" could order someone to do something or to cease to do something (e.g., injunction). In American jurisprudence, the federal courts have both legal and equitable power, but the distinction is still an important one. For example, a trial by jury is normally available in "law" cases but not in "equity" cases.

The distribution of property between husband and wife in a divorce or annulment case. Each party receives so-called “separate property” outright, while “marital property” acquired during the marriage in which both parties have some legal rights or interests are divided between the parties based on the “equities” of the parties (what would be a fair distribution in light of contributions to the marriage, earning capacity, obligations, etc.).
A non-monetary remedy granted in equity, such as injunctions, specific performance, or rescission, available when legal remedies are inadequate.
plainEnglish: A non-money remedy—like making someone do, or stop doing, something.

definition: A body of law developed to address the rigidity of common law, providing remedies based on fairness; also refers to the value of an ownership interest.
plainEnglish: Fairness-based justice that fills the gaps in strict legal rules; also, the ownership value in an asset.

definition: The First Amendment clause prohibiting government establishment of religion, generally requiring separation between church and state.
plainEnglish: The government can't establish or favor a religion.

definition: The total of a person's property, rights, and obligations, often considered at the time of death; also, an interest in land.
plainEnglish: Everything you own and owe—or, in property law, an interest in land.

definition: A doctrine preventing a party from asserting a claim or defense inconsistent with their prior conduct, representations, or judicial findings.
plainEnglish: Being barred from making an argument because of something you said or did earlier.

definition: And others; used in case captions and citations to indicate additional parties or authors beyond those named.
plainEnglish: 'And others'—shorthand for additional parties or authors.

definition: And the following; used in citations to indicate that the cited section continues with subsequent sections.
plainEnglish: 'And what follows'—citation shorthand meaning the cited section plus the ones after.

definition: The legal process by which a landlord removes a tenant from possession of leased premises.
plainEnglish: Kicking a tenant out through legal process.

definition: Any legally presented proof (witnesses, records, documents, concrete objects).
An action or communication involving only one party, without notice to or argument from the other side.
plainEnglish: Done with only one side present.

definition: A hearsay exception allowing statements made under the stress of a startling event, while the declarant remains under that stress.
plainEnglish: Something said in the heat of a shocking moment—an exception to the hearsay rule.

definition: A rule prohibiting the use at trial of evidence obtained in violation of the defendant's constitutional rights.
plainEnglish: Evidence cops got illegally can't be used at trial.

definition: Evidence indicating that a defendant did not commit the crime.
A person named in a will to administer the deceased's estate and carry out the will's directions.
plainEnglish: The person in charge of carrying out a will.

definition: Contracts or leases under which both parties to the agreement have duties remaining to be performed. If a contract or lease is executory, a debtor may assume it (keep the contract) or reject it (terminate the contract).
Property that a debtor is allowed to retain, free from the claims of creditors who do not have liens on the property.
Damages designed to put the non-breaching party in the position they would have been in if the contract had been performed.
plainEnglish: Money meant to give you what you would have had if the deal had gone through.

definition: A witness qualified by knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education to offer opinion testimony on matters beyond lay understanding.
plainEnglish: A specialist allowed to give expert opinions in court.

definition: To completely remove some information from all existing official criminal justice records.
Process by which record of criminal conviction is destroyed or sealed after court order to do so as permitted by statute.

Unusual factors relating to and tending to contribute to the consummation of an illegal act, but over which the actor had little or no control; these factors therefore, reduce the responsibility of the actor and serve to mitigate his punishment or his payment of damages.

The surrender by one state to another state of an individual accused or convicted of an offense outside its own territory and within the territorial jurisdiction of the other state, which, being competent to try and punish him, demands the surrender.

A bankruptcy case filed either without schedules or with incomplete schedules listing few creditors and debts. (Face sheet filings are often made for the purpose of delaying an eviction or foreclosure.)
A circumstance, event or occurrence, that actually takes or took place.
A doctrine permitting limited use of copyrighted material without permission for purposes such as criticism, commentary, news reporting, teaching, or research.
plainEnglish: A defense allowing some uses of copyrighted material without permission.

definition: Any unlawful physical restraint of another's liberty, whether in prison or elsewhere.
The intentional and unlawful restraint of a person's freedom of movement without legal justification.
plainEnglish: Holding someone against their will without legal right.

definition: Using trick or fraud to illegally obtain the property or money of another.
An individual, individual and spouse, corporation, or partnership engaged in a farming operation that meets certain debt limits and other statutory criteria for filing a petition under Chapter 12.

An attorney employed by the federal courts on a full-time basis to provide legal defense to defendants who are unable to afford counsel. The judiciary administers the federal defender program pursuant to the Criminal Justice Act.

As provided for in the Criminal Justice Act, an organization established within a federal judicial circuit to represent criminal defendants who cannot afford an adequate defense. Each organization is supervised by a federal public defender appointed by the court of appeals for the circuit.
Jurisdiction given to federal courts in cases involving the interpretation and application of the U.S. Constitution, acts of Congress, and treaties.
The most complete form of ownership in real property, lasting indefinitely and freely transferable.
plainEnglish: Full ownership of land with no time limit—you own it outright.

definition: A serious crime, typically punishable by imprisonment for more than one year or by death.
plainEnglish: A serious crime, generally one that can land you in prison for over a year.

definition: A legal duty to act in the best interests of another party, typically involving duties of loyalty, care, and good faith.
plainEnglish: A duty to put someone else's interests ahead of your own.

definition: To submit a document to a court clerk for entry into the official case record.
plainEnglish: To officially submit a document to the court.

definition: A document submitted to the court for entry into the case record.
plainEnglish: Any document officially submitted to a court.

definition: One which either terminates the action itself or decides some matter litigated by the parties or operates to divest some right or one which completely disposes of the subject matter and the rights of the parties.
The result of the deliberations of a court.
The constitutional amendment protecting freedoms of religion, speech, press, peaceful assembly, and the right to petition the government.
plainEnglish: The free speech, religion, press, assembly, and petition amendment.

definition: A contract clause excusing performance due to extraordinary events beyond the parties' control, such as natural disasters, war, or pandemics.
plainEnglish: An 'act of God' clause that excuses performance when something massive and unforeseen happens.

definition: The legal process by which a lender takes possession of mortgaged property when the borrower defaults on payments.
plainEnglish: The bank taking your house when you stop paying the mortgage.

definition: The presiding member of a grand or petit jury, who speaks or answers for the jury.
Whether a reasonable person could have anticipated the harm that resulted from their conduct; central to duty and proximate cause analysis.
plainEnglish: Whether a reasonable person could have seen the harm coming.

definition: Falsely making or altering a document.
A doctrine allowing a court to decline jurisdiction when another forum would be more convenient and just for the parties.
plainEnglish: When the court says 'this case really belongs somewhere else more convenient.'

definition: The preliminary evidence necessary to establish the admissibility of further evidence, such as a witness's personal knowledge or document's authenticity.
plainEnglish: The basic showing required before evidence can come in (like proving a witness has personal knowledge).

definition: An intentional misrepresentation of a material fact, made with knowledge of falsity and intent to induce reliance, causing damages.
plainEnglish: Intentionally lying to trick someone into doing something that harms them.

definition: A transfer of a debtor's property made with intent to defraud or for which the debtor receives less than the transferred property's value.
The First Amendment clause protecting the right to practice one's religion without undue government interference.
plainEnglish: The government can't stop you from practicing your religion.

definition: Any person owning an interest in land in fee, including a person owning a condominium unit.
The characterization of a debtor's status after bankruptcy, i.e., free of most debts. (Giving debtors a fresh start is one purpose of the Bankruptcy Code.)
A lawsuit lacking any legal merit or factual basis, often filed for improper purposes and subject to sanctions.
plainEnglish: A lawsuit with no real legal basis—the kind that can get the filer sanctioned.

definition: A doctrine excluding evidence derived from an illegal search, arrest, or interrogation, including evidence obtained indirectly.
plainEnglish: Evidence that came from an illegal search is also tainted and excluded.

definition: Hearing to determine the admissibility of scientific evidence or expert testimony.

One garnished; a person against whom process of garnishment is issued; one who has money or property in his possession belonging to a judgment debtor, or who owes the judgment debtor a debt, which money, property, or debt is attached in his hands, with notice to him not to delivery or pay over to the judgment debtor the amount claimed in the garnishment summons until the judgment in the suit is entered.
A legal procedure by which a creditor obtains payment of a debt directly from a third party (such as the debtor's employer or bank) who owes money to the debtor.
plainEnglish: Pulling money out of someone's wages or bank account to pay a judgment.

definition: The mental state required for crimes where the defendant need only intend the prohibited act itself, without intent for a further consequence.
plainEnglish: Intending the act itself, but not necessarily a specific further outcome.

definition: Honesty in fact and the observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing, often an implied duty in contractual performance.
plainEnglish: Acting honestly and fairly.
related: duty of good faith and fair dealing

definition: A jury that hears evidence in secret and decides whether there is probable cause to indict a person for a felony.
plainEnglish: A secret jury that decides whether there's enough evidence to charge someone.

definition: The person who creates a trust and transfers property into it; also called settlor.
plainEnglish: The person who sets up a trust and puts assets into it.

definition: A secondary promise to answer for the debt or performance of another if the primary obligor fails.
plainEnglish: A backup promise—you'll pay if the main borrower doesn't.

definition: A person legally appointed to care for and make decisions on behalf of another, typically a minor or incapacitated adult.
plainEnglish: Someone legally appointed to take care of and make decisions for another person.

definition: A guardian appointed by a court specifically to represent the interests of a minor or incapacitated person in a particular legal proceeding.
plainEnglish: A court-appointed advocate for a child or incapacitated person in one specific case.

definition: A writ requiring a person under detention to be brought before a court to determine whether their imprisonment is lawful.
plainEnglish: A challenge that says 'the government is holding me illegally—prove it has the right to.'

definition: Unwelcome conduct based on a protected characteristic that is severe or pervasive enough to create a hostile work environment or result in a tangible employment action.
plainEnglish: Severe or pervasive mistreatment based on a protected characteristic.

definition: A proceeding before a court or tribunal where parties present arguments or evidence on a particular issue or motion.
plainEnglish: A court session where a specific issue is argued or decided.

definition: An out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted, generally inadmissible unless an exception applies.
plainEnglish: Repeating what someone else said outside of court, to prove it's true—generally not allowed.

definition: A person legally entitled to inherit property from someone who dies intestate.
plainEnglish: Someone legally entitled to inherit when there's no will.

definition: A person who acquires a negotiable instrument in good faith, for value, without notice of defects, gaining superior rights against the maker.
plainEnglish: A buyer of a negotiable instrument with strong protections—takes free of most defenses.

definition: The court's determination of a matter of law that is necessary to its decision and is binding precedent on later cases.
plainEnglish: The legal rule the court actually decided—the binding part of the opinion.

definition: A special condition the court imposes that requires an individual to remain at home except for certain approved activities such as work and medical appointments. Home confinement may include the use of electronic monitoring equipment – a transmitter attached to the wrist or the ankle – to help ensure that the person stays at home as required.
A neutral word that indicates the killing of a human being by another human being, without giving any idea whether the killing was excusable or felonious.

A witness (also called adverse witness) whose relationship to the opposing party is such that his testimony may be prejudiced; instead of testifying for the party that called him, he testifies against such party; a witness declared to be hostile may be asked leading questions and is subject to cross-examination by the party that called him as if he had been called by the other party.
A jury unable to reach the required verdict (often unanimous in criminal cases), typically resulting in a mistrial.
plainEnglish: A jury that can't agree on a verdict.

definition: About to occur immediately; required for several legal concepts such as assault and self-defense.
plainEnglish: Right about to happen.

definition: To challenge a witness's credibility, typically through prior inconsistent statements, bias, or character evidence; also, the constitutional process for removing officials.
plainEnglish: To attack a witness's credibility; also, the process to remove a public official.

definition: 1. The process of calling a witness's testimony into doubt. For example, if the attorney can show that the witness may have fabricated portions of his testimony, the witness is said to be "impeached;" 2. The constitutional process whereby the House of Representatives may "impeach" (accuse of misconduct) high officers of the federal government, who are then tried by the Senate.
The calling into question of the veracity of a witness by means of evidence offered for that purpose or by a showing that the witness is unworthy of belief.
A proceeding held in private, typically in the judge's chambers, outside the presence of the jury or public.
plainEnglish: Done privately, in the judge's chambers.

definition: Hearing conducted in the judge's chambers rather than in the courtroom.
In the manner of a pauper. Permission given by the court to a person to file a case without payment of the required court fees because the person cannot pay them.
At the threshold; a motion in limine asks the court to rule on the admissibility of evidence before it is offered at trial.
plainEnglish: A pretrial motion to keep certain evidence out of trial.

definition: In the place of a parent; describing someone, often a school or guardian, who has assumed parental duties.
plainEnglish: 'In the place of a parent'—standing in for a parent legally.

definition: Against the person; describing an action or jurisdiction directed at a specific person rather than property.
plainEnglish: 'Against the person'—a case directed at a particular individual.

definition: Against the thing; describing an action directed at property itself rather than a particular person.
plainEnglish: 'Against the thing'—a case directed at a piece of property, not a person.

definition: A person who is not qualified to be a witness.
To suggest guilt.
Evidence indicating that a defendant did commit the crime.
A contractual obligation by one party to compensate another for specified losses or liabilities.
plainEnglish: A promise to cover the other party's losses if certain bad things happen.

definition: To compensate another for loss or to agree contractually to cover specified losses or liabilities.
plainEnglish: To agree to cover someone else's losses.

definition: To formally charge a person with a crime by grand jury indictment.
plainEnglish: To formally charge someone with a crime (by grand jury).

definition: A formal written accusation by a grand jury charging a person with a crime.
plainEnglish: A grand jury's formal charging document accusing someone of a crime.

definition: In a general sense, one who is needy and poor, or one who has insufficient property to furnish him a living nor anyone able to support his or to whom he is entitled to look for support.
Allegation often brought in a habeas corpus pleading alleging the criminal defendant's trial attorney failed to provide minimally acceptable standard of legal assistance.
A formal accusation of a crime filed by a prosecutor, used as an alternative to a grand jury indictment.
plainEnglish: A prosecutor's formal charging document, used in lieu of a grand jury indictment.

definition: One who provides information to authorities which usually leads to the issuance of a search or arrest warrant.
The unauthorized use of intellectual property that violates the owner's exclusive rights.
plainEnglish: Violating someone's IP rights.

definition: Property received from a deceased person by will or intestate succession.
plainEnglish: What you get from someone who died.

definition: A court order requiring a party to do or refrain from doing specific acts; may be temporary, preliminary, or permanent.
plainEnglish: A court order making someone do—or stop doing—something.

definition: In a legal sense, a defendant's inability to distinguish between right and wrong conduct where he cannot understand the nature and consequences of his acts so that he does not have the ability to keep from committing a particular crime.

A defense asserting that the defendant should not be held criminally responsible because, at the time of the offense, a mental disease or defect prevented them from understanding the nature of their act or that it was wrong.
plainEnglish: A defense that the defendant was so mentally ill they couldn't be held responsible.

definition: A state of mind wherein the person knows and desires the consequences of his act which, for purposes of criminal liability, must exist at the time when the offense is committed.
Tort liability for extreme and outrageous conduct intentionally or recklessly causing severe emotional distress to another.
plainEnglish: Doing something so outrageous to someone that it causes serious emotional trauma.

definition: Among other things; used when citing a few examples from a larger group.
plainEnglish: 'Among other things.'

definition: Temporary, provisional, interim, preliminary.
An order which does not decide the cause, but only settles some intervening matter relating to it.
A middle-tier standard of review requiring laws to be substantially related to an important government interest, applied to classifications like gender.
plainEnglish: A middle-level constitutional test, used for things like gender classifications.

definition: When two or more persons claim the same thing (or fund) of a third, and he, laying no claim to it himself, is ignorant which of them has right to it, and fears he may be prejudiced by their proceeding against him to recover it, he may join such claimants as defendants and require them to interplead their claims so that he may not be exposed to double or multiple liability.
Generally, the questioning by authorities of a criminal suspect.
A form of discovery consisting of written questions to be answered in writing and under oath.
A written question served by one party on another that must be answered in writing and under oath as part of discovery.
plainEnglish: A written question the other side has to answer in writing.

definition: Person who voluntarily interposes in an action or other proceeding with the permission of the court.
The condition of dying without a valid will, in which case property passes according to state intestacy laws.
plainEnglish: Dying without a will.

definition: A homicide; the unlawful killing of a human being through recklessness or negligence, but without malice or intent.
1. The disputed point between parties in a lawsuit; 2. To send out officially, as in a court issuing an order.
A factual question that arises in an equity suit because of conflicting evidence. It is an issue of fact rather than an issue of law.

A court-approved mechanism under which two or more cases can be administered together. (Assuming no conflicts of interest, these separate businesses or individuals can pool their resources, hire the same professionals, etc.)
A doctrine allowing the plaintiff to collect the entire judgment from any one of multiple tortfeasors, who must then seek contribution from others.
plainEnglish: When multiple defendants are liable, the plaintiff can collect the full amount from any one of them.

definition: Co-ownership of property in equal shares with a right of survivorship—when one tenant dies, their interest passes automatically to the survivors.
plainEnglish: Co-ownership where if one owner dies, their share automatically goes to the others.

definition: One of two or more persons whose combined wrongful acts caused a single injury, potentially leading to joint and several liability.
plainEnglish: One of multiple wrongdoers whose acts combined to cause a single injury.

definition: An official of the Judicial branch with authority to decide lawsuits brought before courts. Used generically, the term judge may also refer to all judicial officers, including Supreme Court justices.
The position of judge. By statute, Congress authorizes the number of judgeships for each district and appellate court.
The official decision of a court resolving a dispute and determining the rights and obligations of the parties.
plainEnglish: The court's final ruling that ends the case.

definition: A judgment entered against defendant due to defendant's failure to respond to plaintiff's action or to appear at the trail; it is also called "DEFAULT JUDGMENT".
The person who wins an award against some other person in a civil suit.
The person against whom an award is made in a civil suit.
A lien on a debtor's real property that arises when a money judgment is recorded against them.
plainEnglish: A lien on real estate created when a money judgment is recorded.

definition: A list or docket of the judgments entered in a given court, methodically kept by the clerk or other proper officer, open to the public inspection, and intended to afford official notice to interested parties of the existence or lien of judgment.

term: judicial conference of the united states
definition: The policy-making entity for the federal court system. A 27-judge body whose presiding officer is the Chief Justice of the United States.
Court recognition of a fact as true without requiring proof, generally limited to facts that are commonly known or readily verifiable.
plainEnglish: When the court accepts a well-known fact as true without anyone having to prove it.

definition: Colloquial expression meaning to abscond, withdraw, or secret one's self in violation of the obligation of bail bond.
The authority of a court to hear and decide a case, including authority over the subject matter and the parties.
plainEnglish: Whether this particular court is allowed to hear this case.

definition: The study of law and the structure of the legal system.
A group of citizens sworn to deliver a verdict based on the evidence presented in a court proceeding.
plainEnglish: The group of citizens who decide the case.

definition: A judge's directions to the jury before it begins deliberations regarding the factual questions it must answer and the legal rules that it must apply.
Trial of matter or cause before jury as opposed to trail before judge. In a jury trial, the jury decides issues of facts, but issues of law are decided by a judge.

The phrase may mean lack of power to act in a particular manner or to give certain kinds of relief. It may consist in court’s total lack of power to act at all or lack of power to act in particular cases because conditions essential to the exercise of jurisdiction have not been complied with.
The owner of property who leases it to a tenant.
plainEnglish: The owner who rents out property.

definition: The unlawful taking and carrying away of the personal property of another, without force and without consent, and with intent to permanently deprive the owner of it.
Rules and principles of conduct established by the legislature, court decisions, or local customs.
A legal action started by a plaintiff against a defendant based on a complaint that the defendant failed to perform a legal duty which resulted in harm to the plaintiff.
A question that suggests the desired answer, generally improper on direct examination but allowed on cross-examination.
plainEnglish: A question that tells the witness what answer to give—usually only allowed on cross.

definition: A contract conveying possession of real or personal property for a specified period in exchange for rent.
plainEnglish: A rental agreement.

definition: One which is composed of some, but not all elements of a greater offense and which does not have any element not included in greater offense so that it is impossible to commit greater offense without necessarily committing the lesser offense.
The legal seizure of property to satisfy a judgment, tax debt, or other obligation.
plainEnglish: The legal seizure of property to pay a debt.

definition: Defamation in a written or recorded form.
plainEnglish: Defamation in writing.

definition: A legal claim or charge on property as security for payment of a debt or performance of an obligation.
plainEnglish: A legal claim against property securing a debt.

definition: An interest in real property limited in duration to the life of a specified person.
plainEnglish: You own and use the property only during your (or someone else's) lifetime.

definition: A hybrid business entity offering limited liability protection like a corporation while allowing pass-through taxation and flexible management like a partnership.
plainEnglish: A flexible business structure that protects owners from personal liability and is taxed like a partnership.
