definition: Display of a group of persons assembled by the police who are shown to a witness or a victim according to definite lawful standards and procedures whereby the witness or victim is asked to identify the criminal suspect if he is able to do so.
A creditor's claim for a fixed amount of money.
Damages whose amount has been agreed upon in the contract itself, enforceable if reasonable and not a penalty.
plainEnglish: A pre-agreed dollar amount written into the contract for if someone breaches.

definition: The sale of a debtor's property with the proceeds to be used for the benefit of creditors.
A notice filed in public records warning that title to a specific property is the subject of pending litigation.
plainEnglish: A public notice that a property is tied up in a lawsuit.

definition: A party to a lawsuit, whether plaintiff or defendant.
plainEnglish: A party to a lawsuit.

definition: The process of carrying on a lawsuit, including pleading, discovery, motions, trial, and appeal.
plainEnglish: The process of bringing or defending a lawsuit.

definition: A directive issued to preserve potentially relevant documents and information once litigation is reasonably anticipated.
plainEnglish: Instructions to preserve documents because a lawsuit is coming.

definition: A type of advance directive specifying which life-sustaining treatments a person wants or refuses if unable to communicate.
plainEnglish: A document saying which end-of-life treatments you do or don't want.

definition: A judicial officer having by statute some, but not all, of the powers of a judge. These powers include the power to issue arrest process and to admit a defendant to bail.

A judicial officer of a district court who conducts initial proceedings in criminal cases, decides criminal misdemeanor cases, conducts many pretrial civil and criminal matters on behalf of district judges, and decides civil cases with the consent of the parties.
The state of mind which accompanies the intentional doing of a wrongful act without legal justification or excuse.
The premeditation and deliberation, for which there is no justification nor excuse.
The state of mind which accompanies the intentional doing of a wrongful act without legal justification or excuse.
A tort claim against someone who initiated a baseless legal action with malice and without probable cause, where the prior action terminated in the plaintiff's favor.
plainEnglish: Suing someone for suing you in bad faith with no legal basis.

definition: Professional negligence or misconduct by someone holding themselves out as having special training, falling below the applicable standard of care.
plainEnglish: Professional negligence (like by a doctor or lawyer).

definition: Wrong in itself; conduct that is inherently immoral or wrongful, such as murder or theft.
plainEnglish: 'Wrong in itself'—things everyone agrees are evil, like murder.

definition: Wrong because prohibited; conduct that is wrongful only because a statute makes it so, such as traffic violations.
plainEnglish: 'Wrong because banned'—only illegal because there's a law against it.

definition: A writ ordering a public official, government body, or lower court to perform a duty required by law.
plainEnglish: A court order forcing a government official or court to do their legal duty.

definition: A precept or order issued upon the decision of an appeal or writ of error, directing action to be taken or disposition to be made of case, by inferior court. Official mode of communicating judgment of appellate court to lower court, directing action to be taken or disposition to be made of cause by trial court.
A sentence the court is required by law to impose for certain offenses or on certain offenders.
The unlawful killing of a human being without malice aforethought; most jurisdictions distinguish between voluntary and involuntary manslaughter.

Consists of "criminally-negligent homicide" and "unlawful-act manslaughter"; the typical example is where death results from the negligent operation of an automobile; the unlawful act cannot amount to a felony.

An intentional killing committed under circumstances which, although they do not justify the homicide, mitigate it, e.g., in a heat of passion caused by the deceased's provocation, or when the killing, although unintentional, resulted from an unreasonable and grossly reckless conduct.
Title to real property free from reasonable doubt or defect, such that a prudent buyer would accept it; a common requirement in real estate contracts.
plainEnglish: Title clean enough that a reasonable buyer would accept it.

definition: Important, necessary; relating to a given matter.
A breach so significant that it defeats the essential purpose of the contract and excuses the non-breaching party from further performance.
plainEnglish: A breach big enough that the other side can walk away from the contract.

definition: A witness whose testimony is particularly important to the issues in a trial.
The malicious maiming (depravation or disablement of a body part or organ) or disfigurement of another.

Section 707(b)(2) of the Bankruptcy Code applies a "means test" to determine whether an individual debtor's chapter 7 filing is presumed to be an abuse of the Bankruptcy Code requiring dismissal or conversion of the case (generally to chapter 13). Abuse is presumed if the debtor's aggregate current monthly income (see definition above) over 5 years, net of certain statutorily allowed expenses is more than (i) $10,000, or (ii) 25% of the debtor's nonpriority unsecured debt, as long as that amount is at least $6,000. The debtor may rebut a presumption of abuse only by a showing of special circumstances that justify additional expenses or adjustments of current monthly income.
A statutory lien securing payment to contractors, subcontractors, and suppliers for labor or materials furnished to improve real property.
plainEnglish: A contractor's claim on the property for unpaid work.

definition: A voluntary, non-binding process in which a neutral third party facilitates negotiations between disputing parties to help them reach a mutually acceptable resolution.
plainEnglish: A neutral helps the parties try to work out a deal—no decision is imposed.

definition: A writing designed to record an agreement or a set of facts.
The mental state or intent required to commit a particular crime; literally 'guilty mind.'
plainEnglish: The 'guilty mind'—whether the person intended (or was reckless about) the crime.

definition: Special condition the court imposes to require an individual to undergo evaluation and treatment for a mental disorder. Treatment may include psychiatric, psychological, and sex offense-specific evaluations, inpatient or outpatient counseling, and medication.
Being mentally incapable of having the malice, premeditation or other mental state required to find a criminal defendant guilty of certain crimes.
An infant or person who is under the age of legal competence. One under 18.

The rule of law requiring the government to tell a (to "mirandize") suspect after arrest and before questioning that he has certain rights such as the right to remain silent, that the statements he makes may be used against him, his right to counsel and that counsel may be appointed if he cannot afford one.
Warnings required to be given by police to suspects in custody before interrogation, advising them of their rights to remain silent and to counsel.
plainEnglish: The 'you have the right to remain silent' warning before police questioning.

definition: A person guilty of a misdemeanor, one sentenced to punishment upon conviction of a misdemeanor.
A less serious crime, typically punishable by a fine or imprisonment of one year or less.
plainEnglish: A less serious crime, usually punishable by less than a year in jail.

definition: A false statement of material fact made by one party that another reasonably relies on to their detriment; may be innocent, negligent, or fraudulent.
plainEnglish: A false statement someone reasonably believed and acted on, to their detriment.

definition: A trial terminated before verdict due to procedural error, hung jury, or other significant issue, generally requiring a new trial.
plainEnglish: When a trial is ended early without a verdict, usually requiring a retrial.

definition: Those circumstances under which a crime is committed which, while not completely exonerating the person charged, at least reduces the penalty for the offense or the damages arising from the offense.
The duty of a non-breaching party to take reasonable steps to reduce the damages caused by the breach.
plainEnglish: After a breach, you have to try to limit your own losses.

definition: Not subject to a court ruling because the controversy has not actually arisen, or has ended.

A crime of moral turpitude is one demonstrating baseness, vileness, or depravity in the private and social duties which a man owes to his fellow men, or to society in general, contrary to the accepted and customary rule of right and duty between man and man; conviction of a crime of moral turpitude may lead to disqualification from office, loss of licensed employment and deportation of immigrants.
A security interest in real property given by a borrower to a lender to secure repayment of a loan.
plainEnglish: Using your house as collateral for a loan.

definition: A formal request made to the court asking for a specific ruling or order, either before, during, or after trial.
plainEnglish: An ask to the judge for something.

definition: The pleading filed in cases seeking monetary damages. See COMPLAINT.
A pretrial motion asking the court to rule in advance on the admissibility of evidence at trial, often to exclude prejudicial material.
plainEnglish: A pretrial motion to decide what evidence will or won't be allowed at trial.

definition: A request asking the court to throw out a case on legal grounds before reaching the merits, often for failure to state a claim or lack of jurisdiction.
plainEnglish: A request to throw out the case because it's legally defective.

term: motion to lift the automatic stay
definition: A request by a creditor to allow the creditor to take action against the debtor or the debtor's property that would otherwise be prohibited by the automatic stay.

See QUASH. A party uses it when seeking a determination that service of process was not proper and, therefore, the court has no jurisdiction over an improperly served party. It may also be used to stop execution (enforcement) of a judgment where the writ (see WRIT) of fieri facias is defective, judgment has been satisfied, etc.
An oral or written request to the judge to dismiss the case completely because the prosecution has not proven the charges or because of some other legal defect in the prosecution’s case.

The unlawful killing of a human being with malice aforethought, either express or implied; a special form of murder is the "felony murder" where the defendant unintentionally kills or causes to be killed another person in the commission or attempted commission of a felony; Virginia has various "degrees" of murder, each of which has various punishments.
Having changed what needed to be changed. The term is used to draw the reader's attention to the differences between a statement and a similar but different earlier statement.
The agreement of all parties to a contract on the same terms, traditionally called a 'meeting of the minds.'
plainEnglish: Both sides actually agreed to the same deal.

definition: A defense justifying otherwise criminal conduct undertaken to prevent a greater imminent harm.
plainEnglish: Breaking the law to prevent a worse harm.

definition: Failure to exercise the standard of care that a reasonably prudent person would exercise under similar circumstances, resulting in harm.
plainEnglish: Carelessness that causes injury.

definition: A written document, such as a check or promissory note, representing an unconditional promise or order to pay a sum of money, transferable by endorsement or delivery.
plainEnglish: A transferable written promise to pay (like a check or note).

definition: A direct discussion between parties (or their representatives) aimed at reaching agreement, without the involvement of a neutral third party.
plainEnglish: The parties (and their lawyers) just hash it out directly.

definition: A Chapter 7 case in which there are no assets available to satisfy any portion of the creditors' unsecured claims.
(Latin) “I will no further prosecute.” A formal entry on the record of a case by the prosecuting attorney that the charge is dismissed; however, the charge may be reinstated at a later time.
Latin for 'I do not wish to contest'; a plea in which a defendant accepts conviction without admitting guilt, often used to avoid civil consequences.
plainEnglish: A 'no contest' plea—not admitting guilt but accepting the conviction.

definition: A small sum awarded when a legal right has been violated but no actual loss has been proven.
plainEnglish: A token amount (like $1) recognizing a wrong even though there's no real loss.

definition: A contract restricting an employee or seller from competing with the employer or buyer within specified scope, time, and geography.
plainEnglish: A contract that limits where and when you can work for a competitor.

definition: A contract by which parties agree to keep certain information confidential.
plainEnglish: A 'NDA'—a promise to keep certain information secret.

definition: A debt that cannot be eliminated in bankruptcy. Examples include a home mortgage, debts for alimony or child support, certain taxes, debts for most government funded or guaranteed educational loans or benefit overpayments, debts arising from death or personal injury caused by driving while intoxicated or under the influence of drugs, and debts for restitution or a criminal fine included in a sentence on the debtor's conviction of a crime. Some debts, such as debts for money or property obtained by false pretenses and debts for fraud or defalcation while acting in a fiduciary capacity may be declared nondischargeable only if a creditor timely files and prevails in a nondischargeability action.
Property of a debtor that can be liquidated to satisfy claims of creditors.

An oral or written act by a plaintiff at any time prior to judgment which terminates the case without a decision on the merits. The plaintiff may take an initial non-suit as a matter of right; subsequent non-suits can be taken only with the judge's consent.
A public officer authorized to administer oaths, witness signatures, and certify documents.
plainEnglish: An official who can swear people in and verify signatures.

definition: Formal information given to a party about a legal proceeding or matter affecting their rights, required by due process before adverse action.
plainEnglish: Officially telling someone about a legal matter that affects them.

definition: A document filed by an appellant to formally initiate an appeal from a trial court judgment or order.
plainEnglish: The filing that starts an appeal.

definition: A formal notice from a landlord requiring a tenant to vacate the premises by a specified date, often a prerequisite to eviction.
plainEnglish: Formal notice that a tenant must move out.

definition: The substitution of a new contract or new party in place of an existing one, with the consent of all parties, discharging the original obligation.
plainEnglish: Swapping out the old contract (or an old party) for a new one, with everyone's agreement.

definition: A tort involving substantial and unreasonable interference with the use and enjoyment of land (private nuisance) or with a public right (public nuisance).
plainEnglish: Substantially interfering with someone's use of their property (private) or with public rights (public).

definition: Now for then; describing a court action with retroactive effect, as if it had been done at an earlier date.
plainEnglish: 'Now for then'—backdating a court order to fix an earlier omission.

definition: A written or oral pledge to keep a promise to speak the truth.

In legal proceedings, to object (e.g., to the admission of evidence, to a question, etc.) is to interpose a declaration to the effect that the particular matter or thing under consideration is not done or admitted with the consent of the party objecting, but is considered by that party improper or illegal, and referring the question of its propriety or legality to the court; the judge may sustain the objection, denying the admission of evidence, or question, etc., or he may overrule the objection, permitting the evidence or question, etc.
A formal protest by an attorney during a proceeding, asserting that the question, evidence, or argument is improper.
plainEnglish: A lawyer's formal complaint that something improper is happening at trial.

definition: A trustee's or creditor's objection to the debtor being released from personal liability for certain dischargeable debts. Common reasons include allegations that the debt to be discharged was incurred by false pretenses or that debt arose because of the debtor's fraud while acting as a fiduciary.
A trustee's or creditor's objection to the debtor's attempt to claim certain property as exempt from liquidation by the trustee to creditors.
A breach or violation of a criminal law, which is punishable by fine or imprisonment or both, or by death.
A manifestation of willingness to enter into a bargain, justifying another person in understanding that their assent will conclude the agreement.
plainEnglish: A proposal to make a deal that the other side can accept.

definition: A lawyer's statement to the jury as to what he/she expects will be shown at the trial.

A judge's written explanation of the decision of the court. Because a case may be heard by three or more judges in the court of appeals, the opinion in appellate decisions can take several forms. If all the judges completely agree on the result, one judge will write the opinion for all. If all the judges do not agree, the formal decision will be based upon the view of the majority, and one member of the majority will write the opinion. The judges who did not agree with the majority may write separately in dissenting or concurring opinions to present their views. A dissenting opinion disagrees with the majority opinion because of the reasoning and/or the principles of law the majority used to decide the case. A concurring opinion agrees with the decision of the majority opinion, but offers further comment or clarification or even an entirely different reason for reaching the same result. Only the majority opinion can serve as binding precedent in future cases. See also precedent.
An opportunity for lawyers to summarize their position before the court and also to answer the judges' questions.

A direction of the court in some matter incidental to the main proceeding which adjudicates a preliminary point or directs some step in the proceeding; a direction that the court gives to the parties of a dispute commanding them to do or not to do a given act.
A law enacted by a local government, such as a city or county.
plainEnglish: A local government law (city or county).

definition: Oral. Used as a technical term to describe a hearing or pleading which is orally presented.
Jurisdiction in the first instance; jurisdiction to take cognizance of a cause at its inception, try it, and pass upon the law and facts.

To supersede; to annul; to make void; to reject by subsequent action or decision; a judicial decision is said to be overruled when a later decision, rendered by the same court or by a higher court in the same judicial system, expresses a judgment upon the same question of law contrary to that which was given before, thereby depriving the earlier opinion of all authority as a precedent; also refers to a decision by a judge not to sustain or uphold a party's objection to the introduction of a particular evidence or to a specific question.
A judge's ruling rejecting an objection, allowing the question or evidence to proceed.
plainEnglish: The judge rejects the objection—question or evidence comes in.

definition: 1. In appellate cases, a group of judges (usually three) assigned to decide the case; 2. In the jury selection process, the group of potential jurors; 3. The list of attorneys who are both available and qualified to serve as court-appointed counsel for criminal defendants who cannot afford their own counsel.
An exercise of the sovereign prerogative of mercy, relieving the person on whom it is bestowed from further punishment and from legal disability because of the crime named.
A doctrine excluding prior or contemporaneous oral or written statements that contradict or vary the terms of a fully integrated written contract.
plainEnglish: Once you sign a final written contract, you can't bring in earlier promises to change it.

definition: Conditional release from prison before the full sentence is served, subject to supervision and rules.
plainEnglish: Getting out of prison early under supervision.

definition: Permission given to a convicted offender or a juvenile in custody to spend part of his time in the community to learn a skill or to study, although the rest must be spent in jail or in a correctional facility.
The dividing of lands held by joint tenants or tenants in common into distinct portions so that they may hold them severalty; which may be compulsory (judicial) or voluntary.
In a judicial proceeding, a litigant (plaintiff or petitioner on one side, defendant or respondent on the other side), a person directly interested in the subject matter of a case.

A party who has standing to be heard by the court in a matter to be decided in the bankruptcy case. The debtor, U.S. trustee or bankruptcy administrator, case trustee, and creditors are parties in interest for most matters.
A government grant giving an inventor exclusive rights to make, use, and sell an invention for a limited time.
plainEnglish: A legal monopoly on an invention for a set period.

definition: In general, any person who has been given authority to make arrests. Generally, a “peace officer” is a person designated by public authority to keep the peace and arrest persons guilty or suspected of crime and he is a conservator of the peace, which term is synonymous with the term “peace officer.” This term includes sheriffs and their deputies, member of the police force of cities, and other officers whose duty is to preserve the public peace.
The punishment that the law imposes for the commission of a crime.
“Pending the suit” during the actual progress of the suit, during litigation. Pendente lite orders or decree are entered while the suit is pending and are always prior to the final order or decree.
Latin, meaning "for the court." In appellate courts, often refers to an unsigned opinion.
A party's right to dismiss a potential juror without stating a reason, limited in number and subject to anti-discrimination rules.
plainEnglish: Striking a juror without having to explain why.

definition: The legal steps a secured creditor takes (such as filing a UCC-1) to establish priority of its security interest over other claimants.
plainEnglish: The steps a lender takes to make sure its claim on collateral beats other claims.

definition: The criminal offense of knowingly making a false statement under oath in a judicial proceeding.
plainEnglish: Lying under oath.

definition: A court's power over the parties in a case, generally requiring minimum contacts between the defendant and the forum state.
plainEnglish: Whether the court has authority over this particular defendant.

definition: Legal authority that a court may consider but is not required to follow, such as decisions from other jurisdictions or law review articles.
plainEnglish: Law a court can consider but isn't required to follow.

definition: The trial jury that hears evidence and renders a verdict in a civil or criminal case, as distinguished from a grand jury.
plainEnglish: The regular trial jury (as opposed to a grand jury).

definition: A formal written request to a court asking it to grant relief, or some privilege, or license to do an act that requires the permission of a court.
The party who initiates a petition, often the moving party in an appellate proceeding or special proceeding.
plainEnglish: The party making a formal request to the court.

definition: A federal misdemeanor punishable by six months or less in prison.
A judicial doctrine allowing courts to hold shareholders personally liable for corporate obligations when the corporation is used to perpetrate fraud or is a mere alter ego of its owners.
plainEnglish: When the court goes after the people behind a sham corporation personally.

definition: The party who initiates a lawsuit by filing a complaint, seeking a legal remedy against the defendant.
plainEnglish: The person doing the suing.

definition: A defendant's formal response to a criminal charge, typically 'guilty,' 'not guilty,' or 'no contest.'
plainEnglish: How the defendant officially responds to the charges.

definition: A negotiated agreement in which a defendant pleads guilty to a charge in exchange for some concession by the prosecution, such as reduced charges or a lighter sentence.
plainEnglish: A deal where the defendant pleads guilty in exchange for a lighter charge or sentence.

definition: The process whereby the accused and the prosecutor in a criminal case work out a mutually satisfactory disposition of the case subject to court approval. It usually involves the defendant's pleading guilty to a lesser offense or to only one or some of the counts of a multicount indictment in return for a lighter sentence than that possible for the graver charge.
A pleading in which a party asserts that the entire case can be decided on one very specific set of facts which, if true, would decide the case in that party's favor.
To assert a claim, defense, or guilty/not-guilty position in court; also, the act of filing a pleading.
plainEnglish: To formally state your position to the court.

definition: A formal written statement filed with the court setting forth a party's claims or defenses, such as a complaint, answer, or reply.
plainEnglish: The formal documents that set out each side's claims and defenses.

definition: Written statements filed with the court that describe a party's legal or factual assertions about the case.

A collateral product of an illegal search or seizure which is also subject to being suppressed as evidence at trial, e.g., statements made after an unlawful arrest; also called "fruit of the poisoned tree."
Refers to unlawful possession of narcotics or controlled dangerous drugs or marijuana.
A transfer of the debtor's property made after the commencement of the case.
A legal document authorizing one person (the agent or attorney-in-fact) to act on behalf of another (the principal) in specified matters.
plainEnglish: A document letting someone else act legally on your behalf.

definition: A power of attorney that remains effective if the principal becomes incapacitated, used for incapacity planning.
plainEnglish: A power of attorney that keeps working even if you become incapacitated.

definition: A provision in a mortgage or deed of trust authorizing the lender to sell the property upon default without going through judicial foreclosure.
plainEnglish: A clause letting the lender sell the property without going to court if you default.

definition: A pleading used by a party with notice to other parties to have the case called at “docket call” of the first day of a term of circuit court to get a trial date set by the judge.
That part of the litigation process which precedes the actual trial and usually includes pre-trial motions and arguments which ultimately narrows the scope and issues actually litigated.

The arrangement (or rearrangement) of a debtor's property to allow the debtor to take maximum advantage of exemptions. (Prebankruptcy planning typically includes converting nonexempt assets into exempt assets.)
A prior court decision that serves as authority for deciding later cases involving similar issues.
plainEnglish: An earlier ruling that guides (or binds) future cases on the same issue.

definition: A debt payment made to a creditor in the 90-day period before a debtor files bankruptcy (or within one year if the creditor was an insider) that gives the creditor more than the creditor would receive in the debtor's chapter 7 case.

The hearing given to an accused which is held by a judge, to ascertain whether there is evidence to warrant the binding over of the accused on the felony charge to the circuit court for further proceedings.
An injunction issued before trial to preserve the status quo, requiring the moving party to show likelihood of success, irreparable harm, and balance of equities in their favor.
plainEnglish: A court order issued early in a case to hold things in place until trial.

definition: A contract entered into before marriage that establishes how assets and debts will be divided in the event of divorce or death.
plainEnglish: A 'prenup'—a deal made before marriage about who gets what if it ends.

definition: The standard of proof in most civil cases, meaning more likely than not (greater than 50%).
plainEnglish: More likely true than not—the bar in most civil cases.

definition: A report prepared by a court's probation officer, after a person has been convicted of an offense, summarizing for the court the background information needed to determine the appropriate sentence.

The written notice taken by a grand jury of any offense, from their own knowledge or observation, without any bill of indictment laid before them at the suit of the government. A presentment is an accusation, initiated by the grand jury itself. A written accusation of crime made and returned by the grand jury upon its own initiative in the exercise of its lawful inquisitorial powers, is in the form of a bill of indictment.
The legal fiction where one is presumed without any proof whatsoever to have a certain state of mind or capability.

A meeting of the judge and lawyers to plan the trial, to discuss which matters should be presented to the jury, to review proposed evidence and witnesses, and to set a trial schedule. Typically, the judge and the parties also discuss the possibility of settlement of the case.

A function of the federal courts that takes place at the very start of the criminal justice process – after a person has been arrested and charged with a federal crime and before he or she goes to trial. Pretrial services officers focus on investigating the backgrounds of these persons to help the court determine whether to release or detain them while they await trial. The decision is based on whether these individuals are likely to flee or pose a threat to the community. If the court orders release, a pretrial services officer supervises the person in the community until he or she returns to court.
Sufficient on its face; a prima facie case is one with enough evidence to proceed unless rebutted.
plainEnglish: 'On its face'—at first glance, enough evidence to make the case.

definition: Refers to the quantity of evidence sufficient in law to raise a presumption of fact or to establish a particular fact unless rebutted by other evidence; similar in meaning to prima facie case.
An unsecured claim that is entitled to be paid ahead of other unsecured claims that are not entitled to priority status. Priority refers to the order in which these unsecured claims are to be paid.

A party's right in certain circumstances to prevent another from disclosing certain information that party relayed to her by virtue of the special relationship that exists between the two persons, e.g., husband/wife or attorney/client privilege.
The Fifth Amendment right not to be compelled to testify against oneself in a criminal case.
plainEnglish: The right to 'plead the Fifth' and refuse to answer questions that could incriminate you.

definition: A direct legal relationship between parties (e.g., privity of contract), historically required to enforce certain rights or obligations.
plainEnglish: Being in a direct legal relationship with someone (like a direct contract).

definition: For the public good; legal services provided without charge, typically for clients who cannot afford counsel.
plainEnglish: Legal work done for free.

definition: A motion permitting an attorney not licensed in a jurisdiction to appear in a single specific case there.
plainEnglish: Permission for an out-of-state lawyer to handle just one case in this jurisdiction.

definition: A slang expression sometimes used to refer to a pro se litigant. It is a corruption of the Latin phrase "in propria persona."
Representing oneself in court without an attorney.
plainEnglish: Acting as your own lawyer.

definition: Temporary.
A reasonable basis, based on facts and circumstances, to believe a crime has been or is being committed; the standard for arrests and search warrants.
plainEnglish: Enough reason to believe a crime happened to justify an arrest or search.

definition: The court-supervised process of validating a will, administering an estate, and distributing assets to heirs and beneficiaries.
plainEnglish: The court process for sorting out someone's estate after they die.

definition: A court-ordered period of supervision in the community in lieu of (or following) incarceration, subject to conditions.
plainEnglish: Supervision in the community instead of (or after) jail, with rules to follow.

definition: Officers of the probation office of a court. Probation officer duties include conducting presentence investigations, preparing presentence reports on convicted defendants, and supervising released defendants.

A willful failure to observe and/or to comply with any of the terms or conditions of probation; if the defendant is found to be in violation of his probation, the probation may be revoked, modified or terminated.
The degree to which a piece of evidence makes a fact more or less probable, weighed against potential unfair prejudice.
plainEnglish: How much the evidence actually helps prove (or disprove) something.

definition: The constitutional requirement of fair procedures—generally notice and an opportunity to be heard—before government deprives someone of life, liberty, or property.
plainEnglish: Notice and a chance to be heard before the government takes something from you.

definition: In circuit court, it is a book used to record the issuance of process to a sheriff and recording return of process made by the sheriff.
A formal discovery request requiring an opposing party to produce specified documents or tangible things for inspection and copying.
plainEnglish: A formal demand for the other side to hand over documents.

definition: The liability of manufacturers and sellers for injuries caused by defective products, typically based on negligence, strict liability, or breach of warranty.
plainEnglish: Holding companies responsible when their defective products hurt people.

definition: A doctrine enforcing a promise lacking consideration when the promisor reasonably should have expected reliance and injustice can be avoided only by enforcement.
plainEnglish: Enforcing a promise (even without a formal contract) because someone reasonably relied on it.

definition: A written, signed promise to pay a specified sum to a designated payee, at a fixed or determinable future time or on demand.
plainEnglish: A written 'I owe you X by Y date.'

definition: A written statement describing the reason a debtor owes a creditor money, which typically sets forth the amount of money owed. (There is an official form for this purpose.)
Documentation by the person who served the process of how, when, where and on whom process was served.
All legal or equitable interests of the debtor in property as of the commencement of the case.
To charge someone with a crime. A prosecutor tries a criminal case on behalf of the government.
The act of pursuing a lawsuit or criminal trial; also, the party initiating a criminal suit, i.e., the state.
A government attorney who brings criminal charges and conducts criminal cases on behalf of the state.
plainEnglish: The government lawyer prosecuting a criminal case.

definition: A legal limitation on liability requiring that the harm be a reasonably foreseeable consequence of the defendant's conduct.
plainEnglish: The cause has to be close enough and foreseeable enough that it's fair to hold the defendant responsible.

definition: A government-appointed attorney providing legal representation to defendants who cannot afford counsel.
plainEnglish: A government-paid lawyer for defendants who can't afford one.

definition: Damages awarded above and beyond compensation to punish the defendant for outrageous conduct and deter similar future conduct.
plainEnglish: Extra money meant to punish the defendant and warn off others.

definition: An equitable doctrine allowing recovery of the reasonable value of services provided when no enforceable contract exists.
plainEnglish: 'As much as deserved'—paying someone the fair value of their work even without a formal contract.

definition: To vacate, annul, make void, abate or overthrow.
An obligation imposed by law to prevent unjust enrichment, even though no actual contract exists between the parties.
plainEnglish: Not a real contract, but the law treats it like one to prevent unfairness.

definition: Something for something; an exchange of equivalent value.
plainEnglish: 'This for that'—an exchange where each side gives the other something.

definition: A lawsuit to establish ownership of real property and resolve any conflicting claims or clouds on title.
plainEnglish: A lawsuit to definitively settle who owns a piece of property.

definition: A deed transferring whatever interest the grantor has in real property, without warranties about the quality of title.
plainEnglish: A deed that transfers whatever ownership the seller has—no guarantees.

definition: An act of sexual intercourse with a person, accomplished by force or fear of bodily harm or, in any case, without the person's consent; an act of sexual intercourse with a female under a certain age.
Rule limiting or preventing mention of victim's past sexual conduct.
The most deferential standard of review, requiring only that a law be rationally related to a legitimate government interest. Most laws survive this test.
plainEnglish: The easy-pass constitutional test—any half-decent reason will do.

definition: An agreement by a debtor to continue paying a dischargeable debt after the bankruptcy, usually for the purpose of keeping collateral or mortgaged property that would otherwise be subject to repossession.
A doubt based on reason and common sense after consideration of all the evidence; the level of doubt that prevents conviction in a criminal case.
plainEnglish: A real, common-sense doubt—the kind that means a jury can't convict.

definition: A legal fiction representing an ordinarily prudent person, used as the objective standard for evaluating conduct, especially in negligence cases.
plainEnglish: The hypothetical 'average careful person' the law compares your behavior to.

definition: A standard lower than probable cause, requiring specific and articulable facts suggesting criminal activity; sufficient for a brief investigative stop.
plainEnglish: Enough to briefly stop and question someone, but not enough to arrest them.

definition: The introduction of rebuttal evidence. Rebuttal evidence is any evidence that rebuts, counteracts, or disapproves evidence given by a witness or other kind of evidence introduced by the opposing party; rebuttal evidence is offered to contradict other evidence or to rebut a presumption of fact.
A court-appointed person who takes custody and control of property or a business during litigation to preserve it for the benefit of creditors or stakeholders.
plainEnglish: A court-appointed person who manages property or a business during a dispute.

definition: The condition of property or a business being under the management of a court-appointed receiver.
plainEnglish: When a business or asset is run by a court-appointed receiver.

definition: Operation of automobile manifesting reckless disregard of possible consequences and indifference to others' rights.

Rashness; heedlessness; wanton conduct; it is the state of mind accompanying an act which either pays no regard to its probable or possible injurious consequences or which, though foreseeing such consequences, persists in spite of such knowledge.

A condition under which an individual is released (release on one’s own) without bail, upon his promise to appear and answer to a criminal charge; in general it involves only his promise to appear, but sometimes special conditions may be imposed (e.g., remaining in the custody of another, abiding by travel restrictions, etc.).
The act of filing a real estate document (such as a deed or mortgage) in the public records to give notice of the interest and establish priority.
plainEnglish: Filing a real estate document in public records.

definition: A judge's withdrawal from a case due to potential bias, conflict of interest, or impropriety.
plainEnglish: A judge stepping off a case because of a conflict or appearance of bias.

definition: To disqualify oneself, especially a judge from sitting on a case due to conflict of interest or bias.
plainEnglish: For a judge to take themselves off a case.

definition: A procedure in a Chapter 7 case whereby a debtor removes a secured creditor's lien on collateral by paying the creditor the value of the property. The debtor may then retain the property.
This follows cross-examination and is exercised by that party who first examined the witness.
The process of referring to the electorate for approval of a proposed new law or amendment to an existing law.
An equitable remedy correcting a written contract to reflect the parties' true agreement when the writing contains a mutual mistake or fraud.
plainEnglish: Rewriting a contract to fix what the parties actually agreed to but mistyped.

definition: A rule issued by an executive agency under statutory authority, having the force of law.
plainEnglish: A rule issued by a government agency (like the EPA or SEC) that has the force of law.

definition: A written agreement in which one party gives up a legal claim or right against another.
plainEnglish: A document where you agree to give up your right to sue.

definition: Evidence is relevant if it has any tendency to make a fact of consequence more or less probable than it would be without the evidence.
plainEnglish: Whether the evidence has anything to do with the issues in the case.

definition: The act of depending on a representation or promise, often a required element in claims of fraud, misrepresentation, and promissory estoppel.
plainEnglish: Acting based on what someone said or promised.

definition: Sending a case back to a lower court for further proceedings, or returning a removed case to state court.
plainEnglish: Sending the case back—either to the trial court after appeal, or to state court after removal.

definition: The transfer of a case from state court to federal court when the case could have originally been filed in federal court.
plainEnglish: Moving a state-court case to federal court.

definition: A written discovery request asking the opposing party to admit or deny specified facts or the genuineness of documents.
plainEnglish: A written request asking the other side to admit certain facts (so they don't need to be proved).

definition: A discovery request from one party to the other party for such other party to deliver the documents to a particular location for inspection or copying.
Latin for 'things done'; statements made spontaneously during or immediately after an event, traditionally admitted as part of the event itself rather than as hearsay.
plainEnglish: Statements made spontaneously during or right after an event—admissible under various hearsay exceptions.

definition: A doctrine permitting an inference of negligence from the very nature of an accident, where the cause is exclusively within the defendant's control and the accident would not ordinarily occur without negligence.
plainEnglish: Latin for 'the thing speaks for itself'—the accident itself shows someone was negligent.

definition: The doctrine that a final judgment on the merits by a competent court bars the same parties from relitigating the same claim.
plainEnglish: You can't sue over the same thing twice once it's been decided.

definition: An equitable remedy that cancels a contract and restores the parties to their pre-contract positions.
plainEnglish: Undoing a contract and putting everyone back where they started.

definition: The portion of a decedent's estate remaining after payment of debts, expenses, taxes, and specific bequests.
plainEnglish: Whatever's left in the estate after specific gifts, debts, and expenses.

definition: The doctrine that an employer is liable for the wrongful acts of an employee committed within the scope of employment.
plainEnglish: Latin for 'let the master answer'—employers are on the hook for what their employees do on the job.

definition: The party against whom a petition or appeal is filed.
plainEnglish: The party responding to a petition or appeal.

definition: A remedy returning a party to their original position by requiring the wrongdoer to give back what they unjustly gained.
plainEnglish: Making the wrongdoer give back what they wrongly got.

definition: In a divorce action, it is an optional part of the case in which the wife asks and the judge, if he agrees, changes in the divorce decree the wife's married name to her former maiden name. The same result can be obtained in a separate case for change of name.
Adverse action taken against a person for engaging in legally protected activity, such as reporting discrimination or filing a complaint.
plainEnglish: Punishing someone for asserting their rights (like complaining about discrimination).

definition: A document filed with the court confirming that service of process was made, including details about how, when, and on whom.
plainEnglish: Proof filed with the court that papers were served.

definition: The act of a court setting aside the decision of a lower court. A reversal is often accompanied by a remand to the lower court for further proceedings.
The recall of some power, authority, or thing granted or a destroying or making void of some deed that had existed until the act of revocation made it void.
The Sixth Amendment right of a criminal defendant to be represented by an attorney at critical stages of the prosecution, including at trial.
plainEnglish: The right to a lawyer in criminal cases (and to a free one if you can't afford it).

definition: The felonious taking of personal property in the possession of another, from his person or immediate presence and against his will, accomplished by means of force or fear.

A court ruling directing the recipient to appear and present to the court such reasons and considerations as one has to offer why the recipient should not be punished for violating a court order or legal process or for contempt of court.
A penalty imposed by a court or other authority for violation of a rule, often in the form of fines, dismissal, or evidentiary preclusion.
plainEnglish: A punishment imposed by the court for misconduct.

definition: Lists submitted by the debtor along with the petition (or shortly thereafter) showing the debtor's assets, liabilities, and other financial information. (There are official forms a debtor must use.)
Knowledge of wrongdoing or falsity, particularly in fraud cases; an element requiring proof that the defendant knew of the falsity or acted with reckless disregard.
plainEnglish: 'Knowingly'—the requirement that the defendant knew what they were doing was wrong or false.

definition: A file that is physically closed from review. Also a document containing a seal or the word “seal” next to the signer’s signature.

In criminal law, an examination of a person's house or other buildings or premises, or of his person, with a view to the discovery and removal of contraband or illicit or stolen property, or some evidence of guilt to be used in the prosecution of a criminal action for some crime or offense with which he is charged.

An order in writing, issued by a justice or other magistrate, in the name of the state, directed to a law enforcement officer, commanding him to search a specified house, shop or other premises, for physical evidence of an allegedly committed crime, and to bring the same, when found, before the magistrate and usually also, the body of the person occupying the premises, to be dealt with according to law.

A secured creditor is an individual or business that holds a claim against the debtor that is secured by a lien on property of the estate. The property subject to the lien is the secured creditor's collateral.

Debt backed by a mortgage, pledge of collateral, or other lien; debt for which the creditor has the right to pursue specific pledged property upon default. Examples include home mortgages, auto loans and tax liens.
A defense justifying the use of force to protect oneself from imminent unlawful harm, generally requiring proportional response.
plainEnglish: The defense that you used force because you were defending yourself from an attack.

definition: A federal judge who, after attaining the requisite age and length of judicial experience, takes senior status, thus creating a vacancy among a court's active judges. A senior judge retains the judicial office and may cut back his or her workload by as much as 75 percent, but many opt to keep a larger caseload.
The judicial penalty imposed on a person convicted of a crime, such as imprisonment, fine, or probation.
plainEnglish: The punishment imposed after a conviction.

definition: The court proceeding in which the sentence is imposed following a conviction or guilty plea.
plainEnglish: The hearing where the judge decides the punishment.

definition: A set of rules and principles established by the United States Sentencing Commission that trial judges use to determine the sentence for a convicted defendant.
To separate. Sometimes juries are sequestered from outside influences during their deliberations.
The formal delivery of legal documents to a party, witness, or other person to provide notice and confer jurisdiction.
plainEnglish: Formally delivering legal papers.

definition: The formal delivery of legal documents (such as a summons and complaint) to a party to give them notice of legal proceedings.
plainEnglish: Officially handing the lawsuit papers to the defendant.

definition: Allows a governmental agency as judgment creditor to set-off a judgment against a debtor's tax refund to satisfy the outstanding judgment or other debt.
An agreement between parties to resolve a dispute, typically involving payment and a release of claims, ending the litigation.
plainEnglish: Resolving the case before or during trial with an agreement, usually for money.

definition: The creator of a trust; the person who transfers property to a trustee for the benefit of beneficiaries.
plainEnglish: The person who creates a trust.

definition: A criminal offense of taking without force and carrying away of merchandise on sale to the public without paying the purchase price.
Without which not; an essential condition or indispensable element.
plainEnglish: 'Without which, nothing'—an absolutely essential element.

definition: Defamation in an oral or spoken form.
plainEnglish: Defamation spoken out loud.

definition: A criminal offense of bringing goods into a country without paying customs duties on them or bringing in goods which are prohibited by law.
The criminal offense of concealing and transporting aliens into this country who have not been lawfully admitted or allowed to be in the United States.
An inchoate crime consisting of asking, encouraging, or commanding another person to commit a crime.
plainEnglish: Asking, encouraging, or hiring someone else to commit a crime.

definition: A bequest of a particular identified item of personal property to a named beneficiary.
plainEnglish: A will giving a specific item (like 'my car') to a specific person.

definition: The mental state required for certain crimes where the defendant must intend a specific further consequence beyond the act itself, such as intent to permanently deprive in larceny.
plainEnglish: Intending not just the act, but a specific further outcome.

definition: An equitable remedy requiring a party to perform the exact obligations specified in a contract, granted when monetary damages would be inadequate.
plainEnglish: The court orders someone to actually do what they promised, not just pay money.

definition: A trial had as soon as prosecution, with reasonable diligence, can prepare for it; a trail according to fixed rules, free from capricious and oppressive delays, but the time within which it must be had to satisfy the constitutional guaranty depends on the circumstances and the time within which it must be had to satisfy the statutory limits are contained in the applicable statutes.

One where penalty of fine and imprisonment, as provided by statue, is imposed and imprisonment part is suspended and fine part enforced. It is also exemplified in a sentence by which the defendant serves some time and the balance of the sentence is suspended.
The intentional or negligent destruction, alteration, or loss of evidence relevant to litigation, which may result in sanctions or an adverse inference.
plainEnglish: Destroying or losing evidence—usually punished with sanctions.

definition: The level of care a reasonably prudent person (or qualified professional) would exercise under similar circumstances.
plainEnglish: The level of care the law requires—usually what a reasonable person (or professional) would do.

definition: Degree of proof required. In criminal cases, prosecutors must prove a defendant's guilt "beyond a reasonable doubt." The majority of civil lawsuits require proof "by a preponderance of the evidence" (50 percent plus), but in some the standard is higher and requires "clear and convincing" proof.
The legal right to bring a lawsuit, requiring an injury in fact, causation, and redressability.
plainEnglish: Whether this person is the right party to be bringing this lawsuit.

definition: A general order issued by a judge or court that applies to all cases or all matters of a certain type before that court, rather than to a specific case.
plainEnglish: A judge's general rules that apply to every case in their court.

definition: The doctrine that courts should follow precedent and not disturb settled matters, promoting consistency and predictability in the law.
plainEnglish: Courts follow what earlier courts decided.

definition: A series of questions the debtor must answer in writing concerning sources of income, transfers of property, lawsuits by creditors, etc. (There is an official form a debtor must use.)
A declaration made by a chapter 7 debtor concerning plans for dealing with consumer debts that are secured by property of the estate.
A written law enacted by a legislature.
plainEnglish: A law passed by a legislature.

definition: A doctrine requiring certain contracts (such as those involving land, marriage, or performance over a year) to be in writing and signed to be enforceable.
plainEnglish: Some kinds of contracts have to be in writing or they can't be enforced.

definition: A law setting the maximum time after an event within which a lawsuit may be filed.
plainEnglish: The deadline for filing a lawsuit.

definition: A statute setting an absolute deadline for filing certain claims, measured from a fixed event (like product sale), running regardless of when the injury occurred.
plainEnglish: A hard deadline that runs from a fixed event (not when you were injured)—even if you didn't know about the injury yet.

definition: A stopping; the act of stopping a judicial proceeding by order of the court, usually for a limited period of time.

Term commonly used in indictments for larceny (theft); take, steal, and carry away; it denotes the felonious taking and carrying away of the personal property of another, without right and without leave or consent of the owner.
To agree formally on a fact, point, or procedure, typically to streamline the case by removing the need to prove it.
plainEnglish: To agree formally on a fact so nobody has to prove it.

definition: A formal agreement between parties on a fact, issue, or procedural matter, binding on both sides.
plainEnglish: A binding agreement between the sides on a point, so it doesn't need to be argued.

definition: A document in which the parties agree to the correctness of certain statements of fact.
Liability imposed without regard to fault, typically for abnormally dangerous activities or defective products.
plainEnglish: You're liable even if you weren't careless—just because you did the thing.

definition: The most rigorous standard of judicial review, requiring laws to be narrowly tailored to serve a compelling government interest. Applied to suspect classifications and fundamental rights.
plainEnglish: The toughest level of constitutional review—laws almost always fail it.

definition: A process of selecting a trial jury where attorneys “strike” or excuse jurors until the number required remains.
Of its own accord; describing an action taken by a court on its own initiative without a motion or request.
plainEnglish: 'On its own'—when the judge does something without anyone asking.

definition: A court's power to hear a particular type of case, such as federal question or diversity jurisdiction in federal court.
plainEnglish: Whether this kind of case belongs in this type of court at all.

definition: The act or process by which a person's rights or claims are ranked below those of others.
A formal court order requiring a person to appear and give testimony (subpoena ad testificandum) or produce documents (subpoena duces tecum).
plainEnglish: A court order making someone show up to testify or hand over documents.

definition: A subpoena commanding a person to produce specified documents or other tangible items at a deposition, hearing, or trial.
plainEnglish: A subpoena ordering someone to produce specific documents.

definition: The substitution of one party (often an insurer) for another in pursuing a legal claim, allowing the insurer to recover from the wrongdoer after paying its insured.
plainEnglish: When your insurer, after paying you, steps into your shoes to go after whoever caused the loss.

definition: A special condition the court imposes that requires an individual to undergo testing and treatment for abuse of illegal drugs, prescription drugs, or alcohol. Treatment may include inpatient or outpatient counseling and detoxification.

Putting the assets and liabilities of two or more related debtors into a single pool to pay creditors. (Courts are reluctant to allow substantive consolidation since the action must not only justify the benefit that one set of creditors receives, but also the harm that other creditors suffer as a result.)
The constitutional doctrine protecting fundamental rights from government interference, regardless of the procedures used.
plainEnglish: Some rights are so fundamental that no fair procedure can justify taking them away.

definition: Of its own kind; unique and not fitting into established categories.
plainEnglish: 'One of a kind'—doesn't fit any existing category.

definition: A judgment entered without a full trial when there is no genuine dispute over any material fact and one party is entitled to judgment as a matter of law.
plainEnglish: Winning (or losing) the case before trial because the facts aren't really in dispute.
synonyms: judgment as a matter of law

definition: A formal notice to a defendant that a lawsuit has been filed and that they must appear in court or respond by a certain date.
plainEnglish: The official notice that someone is being sued.

definition: Term of supervision served after a person is released from prison. The court imposes supervised release during sentencing in addition to the sentence of imprisonment. Unlike parole, supervised release does not replace a portion of the sentence of imprisonment but is in addition to the time spent in prison. U.S. probation officers supervise people on supervised release.
To prevent the disclosure of discovery of information.
A person or entity that guarantees the debt or performance of another, becoming liable if the principal defaults.
plainEnglish: Someone who promises to pay or perform if the main party doesn't.

definition: A cause of action that survives the death of the injured party, allowing the estate to recover damages the deceased could have claimed if they had lived.
plainEnglish: Damages the dead person could have claimed if they'd lived—pursued by the estate.

definition: The court decision postponing the imposition of sentence upon a convicted person or postponing the execution of a sentence that has been imposed, by the court. When the court suspends a sentence, it retain jurisdiction over the person, and may later set or execute a penalty. When a sentence is suspended the person is usually placed on probation. A violation of the conditions of probation may lead to revocation of probation and return to court for re-sentencing.
The courts’ acceptance of any motion or objection.
A judge's ruling agreeing with an objection, meaning the question or evidence is excluded.
plainEnglish: The judge agrees with the objection—question or evidence is out.

definition: An emergency, short-term injunction issued without full hearing to prevent immediate, irreparable harm pending a fuller hearing on a preliminary injunction.
plainEnglish: An emergency, short-term court order to prevent immediate harm.

definition: Co-ownership where each owner has a separate, undivided interest that can be sold or inherited, with no right of survivorship.
plainEnglish: Co-ownership where each person can leave their share to whoever they want when they die.

definition: A person who leases property from a landlord and has the right to possess and use it for the lease term.
plainEnglish: The person renting the property.

definition: The first day of the period of time prescribed by law during which a court holds session. The docket is set on this day for the session of not set at some other time(s).
Short-hand reference to the famous case, Terry vs. Ohio, whereby police stop but do not arrest suspects because probable cause does not exist to arrest the suspect.
A person who makes a will.
plainEnglish: The person whose will it is (testatrix if female, in older usage).

definition: Oral or written evidence given under oath, typically by a witness in a deposition, hearing, or trial.
plainEnglish: What a witness says under oath.

definition: A person who, although not a party to a contract, was intended to benefit from it and may enforce it.
plainEnglish: Someone who isn't in the contract but is meant to benefit from it and can sue to enforce it.

definition: Legal ownership of property and the evidence of that ownership.
plainEnglish: Legal ownership of property.

definition: The legal suspension or pausing of a statute of limitations, preventing the time from running during the tolled period.
plainEnglish: Pausing the clock on the statute of limitations.

definition: A civil wrong, other than breach of contract, for which the law provides a remedy in the form of damages.
plainEnglish: A wrongful act (not a contract violation) that lets the injured person sue.

definition: A civil claim seeking damages for a wrongful act causing harm, distinct from a claim for breach of contract.
plainEnglish: A lawsuit over a wrongful act causing injury (not a contract violation).

definition: A person who commits a tort and is therefore liable to the injured party.
plainEnglish: Someone who commits a tort.

definition: Confidential business information that gives a competitive advantage and is protected from misappropriation.
plainEnglish: Confidential business info (like a recipe or formula) protected as long as it's kept secret.

definition: A word, phrase, symbol, or design identifying and distinguishing the source of goods or services.
plainEnglish: A protected brand name, logo, or slogan.

definition: A written order issued by a police officer as a substitute for the arrest of the person who allegedly violated a traffic law or ordinance.
A written, word-for-word record of what was said, either in a proceeding such as a trial, or during some other formal conversation, such as a hearing or oral deposition.
An unlawful intrusion that interferes with another's right to possession of property, whether to land (trespass to land) or personal property (trespass to chattels).
plainEnglish: Entering or interfering with someone else's property without permission.

definition: A formal court proceeding to determine the issues of fact and law in a case, conducted before a judge or jury.
plainEnglish: The main court proceeding where the case is decided.

definition: A new trial conducted in an appellate court in which the whole case is retired as if no trial whatever had been had in the court below.

A group of citizens who hear the evidence presented by both sides at trial and determine the facts in dispute. Federal criminal juries consist of 12 persons. Federal civil juries consist of at least six persons.

The endorsement made by a grand jury upon a bill of indictment, when they find it sustained by the evidence laid before them, and are satisfied of the truth of the accusation. The endorsement made by a grand jury when they find sufficient evidence to warrant a criminal charge. An indictment.
A legal arrangement where one party (trustee) holds and manages property for the benefit of another (beneficiary), created by a grantor or settlor.
plainEnglish: An arrangement where someone holds and manages property for the benefit of someone else.

definition: A person or entity holding legal title to property for the benefit of another (the beneficiary), with fiduciary duties to manage it.
plainEnglish: The person who manages a trust's property for the beneficiaries.

definition: A lawyer appointed by the President in each judicial district to prosecute and defend cases for the federal government. The U.S. Attorney employs a staff of Assistant U.S. Attorneys who appear as the government's attorneys in individual cases.

An officer of the U.S. Department of Justice responsible for supervising the administration of bankruptcy cases, estates, and trustees; monitoring plans and disclosure statements; monitoring creditors' committees; monitoring fee applications; and performing other statutory duties.
Beyond the powers; an act outside the legal authority of a corporation, officer, or government entity.
plainEnglish: 'Beyond the powers'—doing something you weren't legally allowed to do.

definition: A defense to contract enforcement where the terms are so unfair and one-sided that no reasonable person would agree to them, often combining procedural and substantive elements.
plainEnglish: The contract is so unfair that the court refuses to enforce it.

definition: A debt secured by property that is worth less than the amount of the debt.
An equitable doctrine requiring a person who has unfairly benefited at another's expense to return the benefit or its value.
plainEnglish: When someone gets a benefit they shouldn't have kept—the law makes them give it back.

definition: A legal action between a landlord or tenant to determine who has the right to occupy the premises.
A lawsuit brought by a landlord against a tenant to evict the tenant from rental property – usually for nonpayment of rent.
A claim for which a specific value has not been determined.
A debt that should have been listed by the debtor in the schedules filed with the court but was not. (Depending on the circumstances, an unscheduled debt may or may not be discharged.)

A claim or debt for which a creditor holds no special assurance of payment, such as a mortgage or lien; a debt for which credit was extended based solely upon the creditor's assessment of the debtor's future ability to pay.
The appellate court agrees with the lower court decision and allows it to stand. See affirmed.
The group of sworn jurors from which the trial jury will be selected.
A member of a panel of jurors; a juror summoned by a writ of venire facias.
The proper geographic location for trying a case, typically based on where parties reside or where events occurred.
plainEnglish: Which courthouse (geographically) is the right place to try the case.

definition: The formal decision of a jury (or judge in a bench trial) on the issues of fact submitted to it.
plainEnglish: The jury's (or judge's) final decision in the case.

definition: Liability imposed on one person for the wrongful acts of another based on the relationship between them, such as employer-employee.
plainEnglish: Being held responsible for someone else's wrongdoing because of your relationship to them.

definition: The process of questioning prospective jurors to determine their suitability and uncover potential bias.
plainEnglish: Questioning potential jurors to pick the jury.

definition: Preliminary examination of a prospective witness or expert by the court or counsel to determine qualifications or admissibility of testimony.
plainEnglish: Questioning a potential witness or expert to test qualifications before they testify.

definition: A transfer of a debtor's property with the debtor's consent.

A nonbankruptcy legal proceeding whereby a plaintiff or creditor seeks to subject to his or her claim the future wages of a debtor. In other words, the creditor seeks to have part of the debtor's future wages paid to the creditor for a debt owed to the creditor.
In modern law, to abandon, to throw away, renounce, repudiate or surrender a claim, a privilege, a right, or the opportunity to take advantage of some defect, irregularity or wrong.
The intentional and voluntary relinquishment of a known legal right or privilege.
plainEnglish: Voluntarily giving up a known legal right.

definition: A written order issued and signed by a judicial officer directed to a law enforcement officer or some other person specially named and commanding him to arrest the body of a person named in it who is accused of an offense.
A promise or assurance, express or implied, that certain facts or conditions are true or will happen.
plainEnglish: A guarantee built into a contract.

definition: A deed in which the grantor guarantees clear title to the property and promises to defend against any claims.
plainEnglish: A deed where the seller guarantees they actually own the property free and clear.

definition: A legal document expressing how a person wants their property distributed after death, typically requiring formalities such as writing, signature, and witnesses.
plainEnglish: The legal document saying who gets your stuff when you die.

definition: A person who testifies under oath about facts they have personally observed or about specialized knowledge.
plainEnglish: Someone who testifies in court.

definition: A doctrine protecting materials prepared by or for an attorney in anticipation of litigation from discovery by opposing counsel.
plainEnglish: Your lawyer's notes, strategies, and prep materials are generally shielded from the other side.

definition: A formal written order issued by a court directing a person or official to do or refrain from doing a specified act.
plainEnglish: A formal court order requiring action or inaction.

definition: An order by the appellate court which is used by that court when it has discretion on whether or not to hear an appeal from a lower court. If the writ is denied the court refuses to hear the appeal and, in effect, the judgment bellow stands unchanged. If the writ is granted, then it has the effect of ordering the lower court to certify the record and send it up to the higher court which has used its discretion to hear the appeal.

“You cause to be made”—it is a writ of execution commanding the sheriff to levy on (encumber, restrict the ownership) judgment debtor's property and “make” (by sale or otherwise as allowed by law) the amount of the judgment plus costs of executing this process (including costs of conducting the sale).

term: writ of habeas corpus and testificandum
definition: The writ, meaning “you have the body to testify”, used to bring up a prisoner detained in a jail or prison to give evidence before the court.

A writ commanding a public official to perform a particular act which is within their public, official or ministerial duty, or directing the restoration of the moving party's rights or privilege of which he was illegally deprived.
A writ from a superior court to an inferior court to cease trying a case because the inferior court does not have the authority to try the case.

A judicial writ, directed to the sheriff of the county or city, in which a cause is to be tired, commanding him that he “cause to come” before the court (subpoena) on a certain day therein mentioned, the member of potential jurors (veniremen) mentioned in the writ of venire facias.

For purposes of appeal to the Court of Appeals, it is an alternative to a transcript of the proceeding as a record of the facts, testimony and other incidents of trial so that the Court of Appeals can be informed of those matters at trial which are now important in the appeal of the case.
A statutory cause of action allowing survivors to sue for damages when a person's death is caused by another's wrongful or negligent act.
plainEnglish: Suing because someone's wrongful act caused a death.

definition: The firing of an employee in violation of contract, statute, or public policy.
plainEnglish: Getting fired in a way that breaks the law or a contract.
